text:
The Coloseum itself is utterly fabulous. Totally magnicent. However…
Trying to book as individuals for any of the special bits, such as the underground tour or the floor of the area is far too hard. I was told by an official on our visit all the big tour guide companies snap the slots up first.

title: Beware of Headout. Its a SCAM!!!
text:
If there were an option to give zero stars, that is exactly what Headout deserves.

I had meticulously planned a once-in-a-lifetime family vacation to Rome from California, something my family—especially my kids—had been eagerly looking forward to for months. Like most travelers, I did my research and found platforms like Headout, Viator, and others claiming to be authorized sellers for major attractions. Given how quickly tickets to iconic sites like the Colosseum and Pantheon sell out, I booked well in advance—over two months ahead—paying nearly $100 per person for the Colosseum guided tour and about $25 per person for the Pantheon.

Everything seemed legitimate. I received confirmation emails, created an account, downloaded their app, and had all tickets readily accessible. Headout’s instructions were clear about the meeting point and arrival time, and we followed them precisely, arriving early and checking in as instructed.
What happened next was beyond shocking.

We were bluntly told that our tickets had been cancelled—no explanation, no prior notice, no alternative arrangement. Just like that, our long-awaited Colosseum visit was gone. My children were heartbroken. What should have been a highlight of our trip turned into a complete disaster.

And it wasn’t just us.
There were multiple other families standing there—confused, frustrated, and equally devastated—who had also booked through Headout and were being told the exact same thing. This clearly wasn’t an isolated incident; it felt like a systemic failure or, worse, complete negligence.
Headout’s customer service was utterly useless. No accountability, no clear explanation, no urgency—just scripted apologies. They couldn’t even offer us an alternative slot for the Colosseum, not the same day, not the next day, not at all. Instead, they casually suggested a substitute tour of Palatine Hill—as if replacing one of the world’s most iconic landmarks with “some nearby ruins” was an acceptable solution. It was frankly insulting.
Unfortunately, the nightmare didn’t end there.
The same issue happened with our Pantheon tickets. Again, cancelled. Again, no explanation. Again, no resolution.

After wasting precious vacation time arguing with their support team, it became painfully clear that it was pointless. All they could offer was a refund—something they are obligated to do anyway. But a refund does not fix ruined plans, disappointed children, or lost experiences that cannot be recreated.
What price do you put on a once-in-a-lifetime family memory that was completely destroyed?

I strongly caution anyone considering Headout: book at your own risk. Having confirmation emails, app-based tickets, and advance bookings means absolutely nothing with them. We had everything in place, and still, we—and many others—were turned away.

Their customer service is cold, indifferent, and completely lacking in empathy. There is no ownership, no responsibility, and no genuine effort to make things right.
I am currently disputing the charges and seeking additional compensation, but the case is still open—and frankly, I am not hopeful.

Avoid Headout if you value your time, money, and peace of mind.

title: Disappointing, plan ahead but beautiful
text: Booked tickets on the official Collosum website which gave and allocated time slot to visit. You have to be in the queue to go in at the exact time otherwise you will be turned away. Our daughter is 18 and I didn't want to risk booking a free child ticket as you have to take your passport to go in. There is a discount ticket which is 2 euro for 18-25 year olds but it's just for EU citizens as the UK is no longer in the EU we got caught out here and were made to buy a full price adult ticket which they would not refund the 2 euros already spent. This resulted in a very disappointing day. This was our second time visiting and we really didn't enjoy our time this time around. We wanted to show our kids the history of the Roman empire but there is nothing to show as an example of what the place was like or what the Romans looked like. With modern technology and AI this could be easily done to help imagine what it was like. They had a screen which we stood and watched thinking it may spark something but it was a complete p*** take as it was just a video showing how they installed the lift!!! The place was crowded and there are lighting cables laying everywhere. The tickets included 24 hour access to the forum and palatine but you could only use this for one entry. Nothing to say how long it would take to see it all. We didn't have enough time to see all of it before our time slot at the Collosum. The forum is run down some of the signs are worn away so can't read them. The plastic wooden effect decking broken and not very good for disabled or people with pushchairs. I was very disappointed as this was the part of Rome that I really loved on our previous visit 20 years ago. We also walked around at night and the lights are really badly positioned and don't light up the areas properly with some things not lit up or lights shining in your eyes. Everything is gated and migrants trying to sell you tat everywhere. Rome although beautiful and lots of history is not what it was. It's dirty and I didn't feel safe especially at night.

title: THE worst customer service. Do not assume you are getting in the Colosseum if you book tickets in advance.
text:
I booked 2 tickets direct from the official website on 2nd Janiary 2025. I booked flights and hotels and was looking forward to our amazing trip to Rome,  for my wife's birthday on 3rd April. I received a confirmation email at the time of booking, and was advised my tickets would be sent a couple of days before my visit. 
Two days prior to the visit, the  venue cancelled the tickets and blamed me for not completing my personal details page at the time of booking. This was a complete lie.
On contacting them, they confirmed I had booked the tickets correctly and that they had been fully paid for. They then told me there was no longer space on my allotted date/time and the error was theirs. They stated that there was no other available spaces that entire weekend and they could not offer me an alternative. 
They provided no explanation.
How can that happen on an automated booking system? I have spent the best part of £3000 in flights and a hotel, for my trip to the Colosseum now to be cancelled 48 hours prior. 
Their customer service has been disgusting. They have finally offered a refund, but that's not what I wanted. I have been denied a chance in a lifetime  visit to this historic site by complete mismanagement and an awful  company. 

Just because you have booked and received confirmation, don't expect that to  mean anything. Its a lottery.

title: Horrible dirty DO NOT VISIT
text:
Enough is enough with the Colosseum! This ancient relic is nothing more than a dirty, crumbling eyesore that’s been hanging on by a thread for far too long. It’s a massive safety hazard, falling apart piece by piece, and yet we keep pretending it’s some kind of sacred monument. Newsflash: it’s old, worn out, and frankly, it’s time to condemn it!

Why are we wasting resources trying to preserve a ruin that can barely stand? It’s a breeding ground for decay, with crumbling stones, graffiti, and years of neglect. Tourists come expecting grandeur but get dust, rubble, and disappointment. The Colosseum is a relic stuck in the past, dragging Rome down with it.

We need to face facts: this ancient structure is no longer fit for purpose. It should be demolished immediately to make way for a brand-new, state-of-the-art facility that meets modern standards of safety, accessibility, and technology. Imagine a venue that can host world-class events, concerts, and cultural experiences — something Rome can be proud of, not embarrassed by.

It’s time to stop romanticizing decay and start building the future. The Colosseum’s days are over. Let’s tear down the crumbling mess and rise up with a modern marvel that truly represents Rome’s greatness today.

title: Disappearing Tickets
text:
What an appalling ticket sales system. 

First you need to bypass the rip-off tours to find the actual Colosseum, be up at the crack of dawn for when they release tickets and then find the right bit to buy tickets. On two consecutive days I’ve tried to buy tickets to visit the Colosseum with friends during our stay in Rome. We wanted to see the underground area as well as the arena and upper floors. Each day I was poised ready to click to buy the tickets but before I could click they disappeared. In a panic I bought what I believed was the right ticket to see all but the underground! 
Basically I have wasted €72 euros as the no compassion ticket “unhelpful ticket service” are only interested in telling you about the terms and conditions! Maybe they are angling to start selling travel insurance, they nearly have as many clauses! 

BE WARNED AND BE CAREFUL

title: Family visit – mixed despite the beauty of the site
text:
We visited the Coliseum with our family (2 adults and 2 children aged 11 and 8).
Booking made on a site we usually use, everything went very well on this side. The meeting point was clear and convenient, and our taxi dropped us off right in front. The explanations in French for how to proceed and where to go were very well done.

However, once they arrived in front of the Coliseum, it got a bit complicated. Despite the designated entrance on the ticket, inside you must mostly follow the movement of the crowd, with the impression that everyone goes to the same place. It’s not very intuitive.

We booked the “Full Experience” ticket including the arena floor, the 1st floor, the Palatine Mountain and the Roman Forum. But the lack of clear indications on the spot has disoriented us a bit.

The audio guide is good in French, which is good, but we found it a bit sketchy and not always very fluid, especially with children.

The site remains impressive and full of history, it is obviously an emblematic place to see. However, we found that there was a lack of presentation and support to help visitors better understand and fully enjoy the experience.

A nice visit despite everything, but which could be better organized and more immersive.

title: Palatine hill not to miss
text: I suggest to buy ticket in advance online, as soon as possible. Saves time and effort. Online it's possible to get a ticket exactly 1 month before. To get guided tour that's tricky online, as all to tours sell out fast. But, even with the 24h visit ticket it gives you an option to see the Arena at scheduled slot and Palatine Hill and Roman forum visit are included (18 euros) - you can visit Palatine Hill & Forum Romanum 24h before or after scheduled slot for Colosseum. One admission only. It's worth it, especially walking the hill and exploring it. If weather suits you it's wonderful thing. You can get audio guide as well ad it helps navigate place and history.

In short, disappointing, not worth it, far too expensive. Even if it is a combo ticket with forum, Palatine and Imperial forums. Another Colosseum ticket may be worth it, this one definitely NOT.

title: Directions? Not existent. Little and poor information about the building and historical events.
text:
According to the online bought tickets you should arrive one hour before your scheduled entry time. Once you get there they don't let you in. You must wait until the booked time comes up. No idea why they make you wait. During December the visitor numbers are very light but crowd control is enforced without reason. There aren't any benches for handicapped people to sit and rest! 
Once you start your tour you will be caught in a chaotic signs and inefficient guiding system. The flow of visitors is not smartly guided, you will feel lost at times. No information available about what you will see. Minimal fractured information about the building and how events were staged. You will not see a reconstruction or model or pictures how visitors over 2000 years ago were seated, just as an example.
All in all very poor organisation, presentation of artifacts, and in general basic information. effective

title: Don’t bother! Observe from outside!
text:
I rarely write reviews but I felt compelled to write this one.
Don’t give the city of Rome your money to see the Colosseum. It just isn’t worth it. It’s overpriced, overcrowded, the staff are rude and there is no system when you’re inside. There are no signs so you walk round in a daze. 

I love history and Rome is fantastic but you are simply unable to absorb this amazing structure properly due to the vast number of people they allow in. It’s all about MONEY and not about the history. It’s unsafe in there  due to the crowds and it’s very clear that Rome doesn’t care about tourists nor do they care about preserving the history of this great city. It’s about profit. Make the most money off bleeding tourists dry, ram it full of people and leave them dazed and confused like cattle on their way to slaughter. 

Believe me, you will get more from seeing the Colosseum from the outside than you will inside and you’ll also…definitely…retain your sanity. 

And don’t even get me started on the Vatican!!! Awful place.

title: Worst Colosseum Ever
text:
Now I rarely ever give terrible reviews. But this place was possibly the worst of all tourist attractions we have ever been to (and we’ve been to a lot).
Now this is somewhere I have wanted to go all my life, but just never got round to it… but on a road trip through Italy so had it on the list.
So… you have to book in advance. Be very aware of this. There will be places they can get you a ticket, but it’s up to 10x the entry cost. The Colosseum doesn’t care about this… is all about the money to them. (Disappointing as it’s the only place in Italy we found like this).
So unless you hit on or pay and extortionate amount you aren’t going to get the best tickets with the best views or access… we resigned ourselves to this. That’s ok. 
But we managed to get tickets for 3.15 on a Sunday. We arrived on time to be ushered to another gate and entered at 3.20. Despite speaking with someone on gate, someone checking tickets, someone else checking tickets, someone on ticket desk and someone on security, no one mentioned they were closing soon. 
Took a few photos and kids went to toilet and by the time we went to go upstairs (3.45) all gates and lifts were locked. Staff explained they were closing. 
A number of rude, sarcastic staff claimed we arrived too late, until I showed them time stamped photos… then they just rolled eyes, walked off sniggering and staring as a group. We were not the only visitors shocked by the attitudes of staff, indeed it was a talking point by a number of people we spoke to as we left. 
Tried to email their team and got a very nasty email as a reply, again lying about time we arrived. I said I had footage (of us waiting for a lift!) and they replied saying I was breaking law if I posted it! 
Certainly a hostile and angry  bunch of people there, don’t quite understand why as have never experienced anything similar like this at any other tourist attraction anywhere in Italy.

title: Attico access was completely amazing! Spectacular and stunning. Quiet and peaceful at the top. Purchasing tickets was very stres
text:
We managed to get tickets to the Attico- upper levels of the Colosseum and honestly it was just amazing.
The scale from the top was remarkable. It was so quiet up there and we weren't rushed at all. The staff on the gate were great and despite our tickets being somewhat staggered times they allowed us entry together.
What an amazing experience!
The reason for two stars is due to the appalling booking system. We literally sat all day 30 days before trying to get tickets every 20 minutes with the site constantly crashing, then having no availability- thus the staggered timings.
Then I found tickets online from a secondary tour operator for over £100 each, so ticket touts are profiteering on the tickets due to a loophole where you can change names once. This should be banned by the provider as I assume bots are being used to buy tickets- which is why its virtually impossible to get them.
Saying that- if you can- its brilliant!

title: Site was good but not the management.
text: We found the colosseum itself interesting and impressive. It was easily to get to on public transport and the queuing and entry seemed to work well. However the booking system was very stressful as getting tickets was a mad scramble to get them into the online basket before it kept constantly changing the availability. Also the security was so rude and rushing everyone. The guard one side of the metal detector was saying "go, go, go" but then the other guard shouted at me because he stopped the person in front of me to search them. Also they didn't tell us the rules for the bag scanner till last second then yelled at us to be quick and they shoved our stuff through with such little care that my mothers property was damaged by being stuck in the mechanism and they didn't even stop the machine. Was a shame because the other staff seemed organised and helpful and professional. The toilets were not suitable for the number of visitors and the shop was way to squashed for the number of visitors also but was reasonably priced.

title: Colleseum rome
text: A tick on the bucket list. Overpriced entry ticket as it was basic. You had to pay extra to visit all. Expect to queue. There is only a restroom at the start and you go one way.

title: Experience doesn't match magnificent building
text:
The Colosseum is the greatest building in the world in one of the greatest cities in the world. And yet this experience is so poor. Driven by profits and ramming as many people through as possible. The owners should invest in a proper experience, they badly let this down. 
Work to do;
- Metro station next door is horrible and dirty. A shambles for the most important station in Italy. 
- Colosseum booking process is a madness scroll of hundreds of websites, some of which are just scams. Thousands of confusing deals on tickets being advertised is just ridiculous. 
- Mad busy. I expected it to be busy of course, but the lack of direction is astonishing. Follow the crowds is the only real way to get round. 
- Totally lacking an immersive experience. Where is the education, where is the view of what this looked like when it was built. 1 TV showing a video on loop is not an immersive experience. Go to Ephesus Museum in Turkey and you will experience what the Colosseum should be like, at minimum. 

I would of course go again. This place is incredible. But the modern experience is simply unacceptable.

title: Beautiful, but expensive and far too many people
text: We wanted to see the Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, so we did. we booked well or in advance with get your guide. But the price was high, we also had a ticket for 8.30 in the morning, we got there well in time and then had to wait until 9.30 before we could enter. Okay, we've seen it, the history is very interesting, but there's nothing else to say about it. I would say: also visit Ostia Antica, also beautiful, but less crowded and cheaper.

title: Get a guide or make sure you have earphones
text:
Tickets were very difficult to get online.

Amazing to see in person.  We had tickets to include the arena, but we missed out on going on to the arena floor as we followed the signs but never found any for the arena, maybe that was just me but I thought the signage could have been better.  

We had the app downloaded but forget our AirPods, no option to purchase a headset inside which is madness as you 100% need information going around, whether its a guide or app.  The vatican museum have the option to purchase a headset guide, disappointed the colosseum didn’t.

title: Dishonest business practices
text: Didn’t realize my reservation meant that I had to go to the Colosseum first, so I walked around the Roman forum for a couple hours, then was not allowed into the Colosseum, unless I paid them another 18 euros. As they pointed out, it said on the reservation (in tiny letters) to go to the Colosseum first. Don’t understand why they don’t have a sign up when you enter telling you go to the Colosseum first, or the  people checking you in inform you, perhaps to generate extra revenue, This scam soured me on the whole experience.

title: Is the work of brain dead or is it just me
text: Apparently the driver's license from the eu is not enough ID to go inside the Colosseum when every rattles and Rome it's valid how is it that cosine the certain point that they need your passport to get inside just remember take a picture of your passport

title: Terrible audio tour!
text: We wanted to use the audio tour like we have done in the past. We took friends that have never been there. The audio tour now is a joke. You are to download an APP onto your phone and do the audio tour through your phone. The APP takes 1.5 hours to download! I have ATT cell coverage and an iPhone 16! There isn't any wifi available. And to make matters worse, the staff there really don't care.

title: Recommend to go in the morning
text: the pizza around there are not that good, i dont think it´s up to italian standard. anyway it´s tourist area so I should not have expected much. I recommend to go there in the morning time because it´s less hot and traffic

title: Well paid and never seen the Colloseum
text: September 3rd I was in a big queue for the inspection of the colloseum; when it was my turn, the man from the inspection said; you are too early, I can't let you in, go do something else. In the afternoon, a little later than what was on my ticket, I was in line for the 2nd time, to which the man said; you are late, you should have reported at 1 pm exactly; in short, half a day gone and money gone.

title: Hot and crowded
text: Was a pain to get tickets on their website, even with timed entry the que was very long, and you need to carry your passport to enter. The structure itself is impressive, but it was so crowded that it is difficult to enjoy it at all. Agree with some of the others- taking it in from the outside was enough. Also, not a fan of carrying my passport around. Perhaps in Nov or Dec when it is not miserably hot the experience would have been more enjoyable.

title: Get a pic from outside that's enough!
text: Its over rated.  Well I really doubt if it's still the same that it used to be.  Too much structural changes.   There are fake sites that have tie up with colosseum that sell entry tickets to arena at high prices but only email you the entry ticket .   Always search for official site for every attraction in Rome.  Daylight robbery I would say, allowing sich fake sites and fooling tourists.  The attraction itself is not worth it.

title: Give the tour guide a miss and don't go whe too hot
text: An amazing peice of history and defiantly has the wow factor. But way o overcrowded to the point u were pushed and shoved just so people could get their photos. Limited toilets, 20minute queues. Didn't see anywhere to get refreshments inside the colosseum and it  was horrendous with a tour guide in 32* heat who had you standing directly in the sun for 10 minutes a time talking and could hardly understand due to broad accent. Outside on the actual grounds no refreshments at all apart from a water fountain. But if u go up stairs to main road there's a few cafes.. if u can get in !! No seating areas at all om the grounds but u can sit on  cold marble like steps.  For an attraction that rakes in over £1000000 a day they could do a little bit more to make it comfortable the public when it's scorching outside.

title: Not a good family visit
text:
This sadly, was the most disappointing trip during our visit. We got there in time for our entry, but there was absolutely no signs to help us find the correct entrance for our tickets and we had to be redirected quite a walk, in the heat, with children. Once in another line, they were quite rude about allowing our children in, as we only had photos of their passports for identification. It was obvious we were a family. Following all of this, we had only 20 minutes to look around the arena floor, but to be honest, in the intense heat and crowds of people, this is all you can really manage with children. 
If you need to use the toilet here, you are still expected to pay, even though you have bought a ticket and the facilities are not pleasant. The man managing the toilet entrance was so rude and took my debit card off me to scan my daughter's through, but kept tapping my card. I had to raise my voice at him, to get him to hand me my bank card back!
I wouldn't recommend this as a family visit, especially in the heat and crowds of peak holiday season

title: Rude  staff and very poor customer service
text: Some of the rudest people and staff I have ever come across. So sad that such a beautiful experience is entirely ruined by extremely rude staff. They need some customer service training

title: No French
text: Splendid place, but have no French nor in the auto guide (except an app on the phone ..) and the signs are in Italian,English and Chinese... But still no French is a shame

title: Line of 3 hours
text: You have to improve the ticket office and the whole line of 3 hours under the sun before entering maybe putting harrowing and tiring shade areas especially if you have children or elderly people

title: Must-see... but perfectible
text:
Unavoidable but disappointing visit on some points
The Coliseum is still a once-in-a-lifetime visit, but the price of admission is really high for what it is. Inside, the shop is overpriced and spoils the charm of the place. Outside, you have to remain vigilant because there are many pickpockets. Finally, the explanations available in French are very limited, which is a shame for a site of this importance.

title: Colosseum security is rude and hostile
text: I had a mini-wine bottle in my purse and they took it away (as they should altho I did not know it was ILLEGAL) but they started yelling at me and threatened to throw me out and call the police. I offered my bad for further inspection but they were not listening, they called the police. The police arrived and said everything was alright and we shall enter the premises but the security kept on yelling at us. It made our trip very unpleasant.

title: Colosseum in summer
text:
Rome always worth a visit.
For this reason, of course, you must have seen the Colosseum. 
Only in the summer do others want to see the 1000send of course.  Seeeeeful full about it. You should plan a whole day for there to be a lot to see here with the excavations all around.

title: Bad experience at the Coliseum
text:
Catch tourists in the furnace; you have to show up 15 min before the time indicated on your ticket so many tourists get turned away when they come early and have to wait on the ground where there is a little shade; really unworthy as conditions.
They treat you like cattle. 
Inside you should better take a guide (avoid Viator because big scam!) otherwise you probably pass by the monument .....
Frankly I much preferred the palatine and the Roman forum right in front because quieter!
I don’t recommend the Coliseum if you don’t like being drowned in the horde of tourists.....

title: Tired
text: Ofcourse  the coliseum is beyond impressive but the infrastructure around it is tired, ageing portacabins for toilets that have not changed since my last visit 20 years ago. 1.4 billion euro every year could make the experience more comfortable

title: Let's downsize.
text:
The Colosseum: imperial glory by day, tourist shack by night.
18 euros to enter, plus another 10 to not die of heat without a bottle of water. Inside? Broken stones, faded captions and a perfect echo for visitors’ blasphemies.
Out? Squatter centurions, selfie stick sellers and hordes of tourists treated like walking ATMs.
Every now and then they even do the haute couture shows: because nothing says ‘respect for history’ like a red carpet on the remains of an arena where you killed yourself to entertain.
But rest assured: 'we are enhancing the heritage'. Yes, I do. With tickets, private events and zero dignity.

title: incredible that in 2025 there are well-known people around who hurt decent people
text: Beautiful place that does not deserve the presence of people such as thieves, pickpockets and crooks. Be careful and do not give confidence to strangers reeds and look like lambs , but they are real wolves , indeed jenes and jackals -

title: Unprofessional
text: A disaster! I booked the tour two months in advance and received a message two days before the appointment asking me to postpone the tour by three days. By that time, I wrote back, I would no longer be in Rome. I asked for immediate notice of whether the tour would take place, but only got a rejection two days later. Nevertheless, I continued to receive telephone reminders of the tour, even though it was cancelled. I have been promised to refund the money, but so far I have not received anything.

title: Too Hot For Summer Visit
text: The Colosseum is definitely an iconic landmark in Roma. However, try to plan your visit for cooler months. I just got back to my hotel about 30 minutes ago. I had booked tickets from the Colosseum website. You can only get the tickets one month from the date that you want to visit. Because I live in Massachusetts, eastern standard time, I had to wake up at 2:30 am in order to book the online tickets at 8:30 Roma time. And seeing the hordes of people in the tour groups trying to jostle for space in looking at the various exhibits in the Colosseum, I would definitely avoid tour groups! Rick Steves' app is more than enough. This was definitely one of the worst experiences for me. The heat and the massive, massive crowds, just ruined the whole visit of the Colosseum.

title: poorly organised, mass tourism
text:
far too many people even taking wire-cut tickets
no/little explanation beyond the mediocre audio guide
very disappointing

title: Something of a disappointment
text: Sure, the Coliseum is impressive but, it is very limited what you can see. I had bought a ticket to go into the arena area, which was a joke, you could only go in about twenty meters and really saw no more than those who paid without this attraction

title: Ein Muss bei einem Rom-Besuch, leider getrübt durch die Einlassbürokratie
text: Das Kolosseum (und das Forum Romanum) sind ein beeindruckendes Muss bei einem Rom- Besuch. Leider wird die Besichtigung getrübt von einer abstrusen Einlassbürokratie und teils unfreundlichen Sicherheitskontrolle. Jede Airportsecurity schneidet da im Vergleich besser ab. Das ist wirklich schade und unnötig. Und trübt das Besuchserlebnis.

title: Rome Trip
text: I visited Italy last september and don't get me wrong, i like history and vintage architecture, but i honestly don't find myself visiting things like this. It is the Colosseum, the one that everyone posts on Instagram when they go in Rome, but it's just not for me.

title: Pre-bought tickets and still didn't get in!
text:
Entrance to the Colosseum is completely chaotic! We pre-bought tickets for the Roman Forum and Colosseum weeks before our trip and chose a specific time from the timeslots that were available. 

Entrance to the Roman Forum was fine, just long lines depending on the time of day and which entrance you choose. I can recommend going away from the Colosseum and using other entrances where the line is usually much shorter.

The Colosseum tickets say to arrive 15 minutes before your time slot. We had chosen 12:15 and arrived just before 12:00, only to be met with a massive line with absolutely no organisation. We went to the front where people were actually being admitted and had to distract one of the staff scanning tickets to try and get information - absolutely nobody is there to answer questions or help, despite the large crowd of people who were confused and unsure. Apparently everyone just joins the same single line, regardless of the time slot they have reserved, and I watched her admit people who are booked at 13:00 or even later! What is the point of time slots if they are not adhered to? When I asked what happens if we miss our timeslot, she could not give a clear answer and just told us to join the line. We ended up not even bothering, as by our estimate the line would take at least 40 minutes and the entire thing is in direct sun.

I can only leave a 1 star review as our tickets didn't even get us inside. A waste of time and money in regards to the Colosseum. There seems to be far too many questionable aspects about visiting the Colosseum, from scam ticket websites to zero organisation or consideration for people's experience. Whoever is responsible needs to do something to clear up what should be the icon of any trip to Rome.

title: Exhausting on hot days, but still interesting
text:
- obviously impressive
- too many tourists
- super hot -> especially when visiting in summer (be prepared)
- audioguide was good, but not especially made for younger children (very detailed facts)

title: Vivicos through Viator, NOT recommended!
text: Vivicos through Viator provide a copy of barcode to Colosseum for €50 pp. DO NOT BOOK. Tour booked for 10 am deferred for "operational reasons" until  11. No guide to be seen with company logo Vivicos. Audio did not work for all group members. Very unsatisfactory experience!

title: Must have seen more but also not
text: First of all. You must have seen it but not as spectacular as the Roman Forum. Entrance control fully exaggerated

title: Beautiful but Unorganized
text: It was a nice view but I thought the place was very unorganized and confusing to navigate around. Overall, it is a nice place to visit and learn about the history of the city.

title: Over crowded
text: It was a complete Zoo with thousands of people spoiling the experience. I now know what over tourism means. It is amazing but try and go off season!

title: Check ticket carefully
text: My rating is for the ticket sales not the site, that is amazing and well worth the visit. However, we bought our tickets on the day at the forum entrance around 10.15, and were told our colleseum time was 12.15 but be there about half hour before. As I cannot walk great we did a little of the forum expecting to be able to go back afterwards but we couldn’t and this was not explained at all at the ticket booth😡 if we had known we would have walked to the other side and do the colleseum first as the forum is a good 2-3 hours to get round. We complained but to no avail, and had to pay again to get back in

title: Sight-seeing.
text:
The Colosseum is undeniably a must-see when visiting Rome. The sheer scale and history of the structure are awe-inspiring, and it's incredible to stand in a place with so much ancient significance. The audio guide and signage provided some helpful context, making it easier to imagine what it was like during its prime.

That said, the experience was a bit hampered by the massive crowds and long lines—even with timed tickets. It felt a little rushed and hard to fully enjoy the atmosphere with so many people around. Also, parts of the site were closed off during our visit, which was disappointing.

Overall, it’s absolutely worth seeing for the history alone, but I’d recommend going early in the morning or booking a guided tour to make the most of it.

title: Underwhelming
text:
Actually quite disappointed either way this. Massive queues to get in and just rammed everywhere.
It’s interesting for about 10 mins then you’ve seen it.
Better from the outside.
Our app didn’t work either which didn’t help.

title: Never again!
text: Absolute bedlam. Rome is over touristed and the school groups are ill mannered and clutter up the place. Too many groups wandering around en masse. Impossible to get a shot without people in it. I will never go back.

title: Amazing building but way to crowded to enjoy.
text:
The building itself was amazing to see if you could get a good look from the viewing areas. We were disappointed in how many people they let in, they herd you in like cattle. It is so crowded on the inside it's difficult to get to the viewing areas without pushing yourself towards the front. To many so called influencers setting up their tripods and doing selfies are in the way of people just wanting to look around.
Be best if they limited how many people at once were in the place.

title: Amazing experience
text: Too much visitors was there when I visited that place. But sightings was amazing, great opportunity to observe ancient things

title: Ruined experience
text: It’s fascinating. The structure and design is fascinating to look at, the monument itself is spectacular when you re In front of it. However, our experience was ruined by a Chinese tourist who repetitively moved us out of view of her selfie. Extremely rude and pushed her way to the front and actually moved my husbands arm and pushed him back out of her view. She was there for ages trying to get the right shot. People taking selfies and people with selfie sticks ruin it for others as views become restricted.  There should be a one way policy around the coloseum. Literally shoulder to shoulder and in the heat it is very uncomfortable.  Toilet queues are long, limited spaces to sit and take a break. A lot of security to get through too which is a good thing but be prepared to queue. A lot of staff that just stand there, they could manage the crowds better. It took us about 1.5 hours to complete, you could spend all day there but it was just extremely busy and hot.

title: Terrible for babies and breastfeeding
text:
Review with a baby.

The actual colosseum is fantastic. A wonder of architecture.

I visited with my baby (8months) and I just found the whole experience very difficult.

They suggest baby carriers rather than prams. Take your pram. It’s a nightmare in a carrier as there’s nowhere for babies to shelter from the sun whereas a pram would have the sun shade. It’s like going to a football match, shoulder to shoulder with people so I think a pram would be safer for baby.

The floors were smooth enough for any stroller and there are lifts and if you can find them separate baby/pregnant/disabled exits.

The staff were tired and unhelpful. The signage was crap.
Toilet queue was massive.
There are little to no benches.

The website advertises a place for breast feeding. There is no signage to this and when I asked they said it doesn’t exist anymore.

I know it’s an old structure but I feel the capacity of people entering is too much and you can’t really enjoy it because of how busy it is.

The official website is confusing too. I bought a ticket and didn’t get access to what I expected. I asked if I could pay the extra €4 or upgrade or buy a new one and was told no.

title: Buy from Colosseum's website not here!
text: We were fooled by TripAdvisor when we bought a ticket. It said they had a ticket and I bought them for me and my girlfriend. When we were to pick up those tickets the day we were going to see, we were told that those tickets were sold several weeks ago. Buy in good time and buy from Colosseum's website.

title: To do
text:
We were a little disappointed that a lot of the ground floor is hidden due to work.
Nevertheless, you must discover this place which is a must.
The staff in charge of the entrances a little unpleasant

title: Do NOT book with Viator
text:
Colossuem itself was fantastic - but there is NO signage. No one to assist. No one to help. No one to tell you what lines to line up in. No one selling tickets. No admission point. No toilets outside. Nothing to do while lining up. 

Our admissions meet up person from VIATOR was late and it was an absolute waste of time waiting for them. All they do was give you a QRcode - why can’t they just email it ???

title: Run away if you don't like crowds!
text: I was there 37 years ago. I couldn't find the magic. It's crowded, crowded, crowded. There was an exhibition on Gobekli Tepe... nothing to do, weird, why the choice? I put 3/5 because it remains an impressive building but I wonder if it is worth going into...

title: A Bit Disappointed
text:
We had a tour of Colosseum on our own, without a guide. But we booked our tickets via Tiqets days before our trip to Rome. It was a wise decision because honestly, if we were there without any prior preparation, we wouldn't know what to do, where to go, how to find the ticket office: it is that crowded, even in March!! However, Tiqets office was quite far from the Colosseum (nearby the Roman Forum entrance), so the walk was a bit exhausting and on top of it, though we bought the tickets with arena access, the day we were there, we are told arena access is not possible due to overbooking. We are still waiting the reimbursements for that part of the ticket. 

Anyway, other that these 2 setbacks, entrance to Colosseum was easy thanks to Tiqets tickets: we didn't have to wait in the queue (entrances were time based anyway), security checks were pretty swift as well. But the Colosseum itself was a bit disappointing, especially having been to famous El-Jem in Tunisia where you can access all parts of the arena which makes the experience all the more unforgettable. In Colosseum all you get is the scuffle of masses. 

So, in case you're not that much into the Colosseum, watching it from outside will also suffice. Palatine Hill and Roman Forum are definitely much more interesting.

title: Interesting - One and Done
text: We felt the Colosseum was more interesting from the outside, and possibly better preserved.  We were on a tour, and the guide was helpful in describing how it might have been.  March 2025 it was in various degrees of renovation, as is much of everything in Rome.  The crowds were significant, even in early March.  I enjoyed walking around it in the early morning and at night when the crowds were gone.  It was interesting to learn the Romans removed the marble that, no doubt, made it all the more impressive.  They used it for the Vatican.  So there's that....  I'm glad we went but it's definitely a "one and done".  We did go in the Gladiators Entrance which was interesting to see the perspective from the "floor".  Since modern stadiums are so large, it didn't seem as imposing.  But for that period of time, its quite impressive.

title: Colosseo ticketing scam is rife. Staff is enforcing exact name match with ID.
text:
Got denied entry because my online ticket has my initials instead of my first names. The young man insisted that my exact full name should be present on the ticket, as it appears on my ID, regardless of the ticket validity, of my proof of payment, etc.

I went to the booth to buy another pair of tickets, talking to staff about this nonsense. They insisted that I buy new tickets, even if my valid ticket had a minor inconsistency on the full name part. Then, I was able to enter without the staff even looking at my names. It does strongly feel like the colosseo staff is aware of scamming/scalping websites leveraging the colosseo's popularity, and actively participate in that scam. They also know about the many online scalpers but don't bother taking them down or closing their APIs to them.

The site of fantastic. What engineers did 2000 years ago made me forget how present-day Rome residents are abusing their legacy.

title: Awful experience.
text: Never trust the people on the way out when my 8-year-old son had to go to the bathroom on the way out we were told to go to the bathroom outside because the one inside was so far away and we were told that with the tickets 🎟️ we could go back in. When we tried to get in again they told us no, that we were not. We were very little time inside, experience of grief. They don't have claim sheets. Quite a mess, we feel cheated.

title: Very degraded interior
text: There is no audio guide in French, nor anything described in French. You have to master English to learn things on the spot. The exterior is impressive. The interior is very degraded. There are no more bleachers. You have to look at the models to image the site before the damage. It remains a beautiful visit, for history, but not to learn more.

title: Colosseum rome
text: The colosseum this time round was nice but not as good as 5 years ago. The trust or government have cottoned on to its a big money earner and try to get you through as fast as possible. The staff are not as polite or intrested in any sort of help it seams they are only there for the pay cheque and your interrupting their conversation. You are now put on a one way system that directs you out out out as the staff say out. They have closed off a lot more of the areas that are not on the one way system I understand that in some areas they are doing workes and that's OK but in others areas  it's now staff only where you use to be able to go and admire the engineering and beauty. And this one way system I keep harping on about with a young family half way round wanting to use the toilets we made our way down near the end and asked to use the toilet as you can't just walk to them only at the beginning is this posible. We were told go out the exit. I asked do we then go back in the entrance they said no just get out I did explain we had only done half the experience and just needed the loos and their reply was it's tought you have to go out. I took the family the wrong way round to get back to the begging being shouted at that I was not aloud I ignored this and continued your rude i get rude then at the beginning I asked if we could just exit as we wanted to leave meet with no you can't you have to go all the way back round the one way system. I'm not say don't go it's beautiful but plan you visit if you need the loos go back down the wrong way to the beginning and don't forget to get your tickets to the underground gladiators area and the plebian / plebs (poor person) view. You use to be able to get on to the stage but this is extra now like I said earlier they are now charging for every little extra. Take ear phones to do the talking points a member of staff i asked to hire where they use to do it just said no and pointed to a QR code. I will go again in the future but plan a bit or lot better and hopefully a lot of the building renovation will be done. Just a little note Palatine Hill a lot of the rooms with statues are ticketed so again plan before it's a long way back to the start to get these. So in a nutshell plan plan plan

title: Be on time or no entry!
text: Make sure to arrive at the time allocated. Ticket line was over 2 hours, stated time for entry 2pm. Unfortunately, having arrived in Rome that morning had not changed my watch to local time  - they would not let me in - even as a solo visitor.  Surely they could show some leeway!!!!

title: Lost in Rome~
text:
The historical sites (Colosseum, Roman Forum, Trevi Fountain...) are magnificent but the problem lies in the signage in Rome. Everything is announced at the last minute: you will find the exits before you have even started the visits, but indications of the direction of visit or precise places are almost non-existent (or so, but once you arrive in front of the monument having managed thanks to Maps...).
It is heartbreaking that such a beautiful and famous historic city has such deplorable signage...

title: A hoax!
text: A complete fraud!!!!! Do not buy anything through this operator, it charges more than twice for tickets and for minors who when you get there do not pay!! They don't serve you tickets, you have to buy others and they don't give you back

title: Great location - absolutely worth seeing
text: Very nice but of course tourist magnet, therefore always very many people. So you have to bring time and patience.

title: Viator ( Dreamtours ) colosseum tour
text:
Paid for a guided tour 6 Adults and 3 Kids and met agent for ticket's before tour and entrance to site .
Tickets where sent via WhatsApp and we were refused entry as ticket's where invalid 
We rang guide and he apologised and said he will refund 
The colosseme staff where very good and we rebooked with them 
Travelling from Ireland and prepaid with Viator ( Dreamtours ) its adisgraceful that this happened 
Do not use as very stressful 
Lorcan Dublin Ireland

title: Make Sure you have photo ID
text:
We visited the Collosium recently. Please dont do what we did. Waited in the queue for entry tickets for 30mins got to the kiosk and we were asked for photo ID for entry.
I had my drivers licence with me but my partner never had any photo ID, so we were refused entry. Carry photo ID for entry guys.

title: POOR MANAGEMENT
text:
MY REVIEW IS PURELY ABOUT THE MANAGEMENT.
In Rome with the family, in the first days of January.
Unable to make the reservation online.
At 10 am in the pits you have to queue for more than 2 hours just to buy your ticket, which then does not allow you to enter immediately, but to have to queue for another kilometer.
Too bad because my daughter's wish was to visit the Colosseum from the inside, she had to be content to see it from the outside

title: Colosseum
text:
Far too many people, in front of guided groups
You don't get to see much due to the many groups
Rude staff
Poor regulation to get out
On the whole disappointing 
But still something to see

title: Largely side visit and disappointing
text: Very overrated. Prices are unclear. Very little explanation or indication of the history of the monument. Visits to the basements and the 3rd floor are extras. Very disappointed.

title: Watch which stairs you take!!!!!
text:
We bought ticket for 1. and 2. Floor. 
After 1 hour I looked for a toilet which I saw was at 1. Floor. I went down stairs to find the toilet and suddenly I was not allowed to go back up to 2. Floor. By some employees standing by the end of the stairs. 
 
Why not make I more clear if you are going somewhere and are not allowed to go back???!

title: Be careful where you buy your tickets!
text:
The Colosseum is a must do visit - but be careful where you buy tickets

The Colosseum itself is awesome, as are the Forum and Palotine Hill. Be CAREFUL how you buy your tickets though. The basic €18 ticket, available from the official website, enables you to choose a time and skip the line. Don’t be fooled into thinking you’ll get something different by paying more (unless of course you have a guide, and I’m sure they are very good). I paid €30 to Rome Tickets which looks like an official site - for the €18 ticket and nothing more!

title: Difficult route due to the crowds
text:
The place is unmissable of course. It’s beautiful but the route inside is very complicated when there are people and yet the tours are booked on time slots. 
Overall the visit is not pleasant and therefore we move quickly and without pleasure.

title: Be very careful booking tickets online from official site, very rude staff
text: The Colosseum is without doubt one of the wonders of the world , incredible place but out visit was spoiled by ridiculous pettiness and very rude staff. I’d booked two Colosseum experience tickets online at a cost of 48 euro . The tickets were both in my name , a clear mistake as my wife and I were visiting. On presenting our tickets at the entrance a very rude arrogant member of staff said there was nothing that could be done  and told us the buy another ticket .We went to ticket office and appealed to the ticket seller and again the girl was very rude , unhelpful and arrogant . Who ever runs the staff at the Colosseum take a look at your staff , on the main young , bored , unhelpful, surly and arrogant. Apparently you can change the name on the ticket but not less than 24 hours in advance, no good when you turn up on the day with your tickets , be very careful booking online

title: Squashed in
text:
After touring Castel Sant Angelo the day prior, this place as a disappointment in terms of the overall experience.

Obviously it is tremendously busy and I couldn’t tell you how to make it less chaotic than it is, but be under no illusion, it is chaos. Be sure to book a ticket in advance and take your passports as these will be checked. 

People are just totally crammed in - I get it, the place is huge and can fit plenty of people but it was just so unpleasant. I was glad for decent security screening (airport style).

The views from the upper level across the arena are good, excellent really,  and there is full access up there, but again it is packed full. Tour group upon tour group shuffling about with headphones in. 

I’m glad I’ve been and I’m glad my kids have seen it, it is worth doing but the experience wasn’t fun and I can’t foresee a circumstance that I would go back.

Tip - if you are also doing Forum and Palatine Hill, head down the street a little for access there. There’s still a queue but not as big as the one closer to Colosseo.

title: Bad service ever!!!
text:
If possible, I wouldn't give a single star! Worst service ever!
We booked tickets for the Colosseum through Viator (€179 for 3 adults!) and showed up at the announced redemption point 15 minutes before! The queue was so long that it took us more than 45 minutes to get to the only employee on site, who unfortunately had to tell us that our tickets were not there! Instead of dealing with the matter, we were literally left behind and other customers served; only after decisive inquiries on our part did she try to find a solution. At 11.15 we finally got a mail with the tickets and 1 minute later another one with the note our tickets had expired! I have to say that I especially Considering the price, have never experienced a worse service! 
So the visit to the Colosseum never happened for us despite almost €180 and I will never book with Viator again! What a shame!

title: Take photo ID
text: I’ve wanted to visit the Colosseum from being a small child and couldn’t wait to visit. Having waited in the queue ( myself and my daughter had pre booked tickets) we showed them to two young men manning the entry to then be asked to provide ID. We didn’t have any on us as we hadn’t seen anything about bringing ID on the booking app. My daughter said she had proof of purchase on her banking app and one of the men said that would be ok, for my daughter to show him and him snigger at her and say “no” photo ID only !!! At this point people were walking by and looking at us which wasn’t nice as my daughter was upset. Luckily my husband was at home and could send us photo ID from home. The other man let us in straight away. This put a damper on our visit. The colosseum itself was fantastic but very crowded and the amenities weren’t good either.

title: Ruined by rude staff
text:
I enjoyed my visit to the Roman Forum I felt underwhelmed with the Colosseum. I booked the first time slot. 
However, My digital ticket did not say I had to bring my passport so I did get turned away at first. 
I do believe the staff could handle it better rather than being extremely rude and abrupt. The staff member I went to first kept saying “passport “. 
I then explained I could log into my bank to prove my identity. He said “yes show me” , he stood and watched as I logged into my banking to prove my name matched the ticket, he then did a chuckle and went “no”. 
All this whilst people were watching me. 
The second member of staff still wasn’t the nicest but explained it better to me, he allowed me to stand to the side and get a photo of any photo id I had. I eventually showed a picture of my drivers license. 
The staff are really cold and unwelcoming unfortunately it put me in such an upset  mood and tainted my experience as I felt I had been made a spectacle of.

title: They are not responsible
text: 0 recommended unless confirmed tickets at checkout. We bought our tickets three days ago and on the day of booking they have been cancelled citing a system problem. We have not been given any solution except the refund of the money and have been wasted a full day of travel to Rome. Company nothing serious.

title: Exterior (and night) beautiful, Overrated interior
text: From the outside, it is exceptional at night and beautiful by day. On the other hand, the interior is very disappointing, especially because of the crowds! Too many people! We're literally walking over each other, and yet they added slots to regulate... but no, still so many people, and it was late October. So, to see something, it’s complicated: you have to wait, you get pushed... Not very pleasant as a visit. Instead, I recommend taking the time to visit the Roman Forum and the Palatine Mountain, which are much more beautiful.

title: Absolute snorefest
text:
This trip was incredibly underwhelming. When I was told that I was visiting the colosseum I was brimming with joy, yet the tour guide was so uninteresting that I could’ve fell asleep right then and there.

Unless you wish to see the building and the inside, I highly recommend avoiding this attraction.

title: No facilities, overpriced.
text: Massive queue for the toilets near the entrance, so decided to wait to find alternative. However once you’ve gone upstairs there’s no further access to the toilets, there’s only the one set at the entrance. Had to leave early to find public toilets outside and still queue for ages to spend €1.20 for stinking filthy toilets.

title: The coliseum is beautiful. Visit by the shameful escort.
text:
We booked for free access to the coliseum underground, not having been able to book the guided tour. 
On the site, we are offered to download the application to have an audio guide for the visit.
On D-Day, it is difficult to find the place to go to access the underground because there is no indication. 
We'll have an escort with us. He cuts us brutally and quite violently several times while listening to the audio guide (available only in English and Italian) and ends up aggressively telling us that the visit is in all of 3/4h. Reservation site does not indicate it, the confirmation email, the tickets and him at the meeting point neither, he always replies aggressively that "it is not written anywhere but the guides know it" (SIC!) and "as there are many people, we must reduce the visit time" (re-SIC!). 
If there are too many people, sell fewer tickets but it is not up to tourists to have - time available on the site.
Given the Award of the ticket and the number of people visiting the coliseum daily, it also seems to us that an audio guide in several languages could be proposed. 

The ticket also includes access to the forum but you should be careful about the opening hours of the different sites provided in the ticket (information at the entrance to the forum would be welcome)

The Colosseum and the Forum are magnificent but with this Rating we would like to draw attention to the difficulties encountered and especially to the attitude of some staff members.

title: An exemplary tourist trap!
text: You have to buy a ticket to get in. I have no problem with that. But if you go even 5 minutes past the time written on your ticket, they won't let you in. In a city like Rome, where transportation and traffic are terrible, delays are inevitable. The staff is completely unhelpful and treats you like a dog. They want you to buy a ticket again. There's nothing this stupid! With the same ticket, you can enter the Palatine Hill or the Forum Romano at any time you want, but you can't enter the famous Colosseum! I've never seen or heard of such a ridiculous practice anywhere in the world! If we were to say let's buy a ticket again, there's an incredible queue there too. I don't think tourists are treated like dogs anywhere else in the world. Rome is already an exaggerated bubble. And every corner is full of tourist traps. And the most magnificent of these is the magnificent super uber Colosseum.

title: SUPER MASSED
text:
It ran at the beginning of the 90s of the last century and my wife and I visited the Coliseum inside practically alone for a few hours and nowadays visiting Rome on 3/10/2024 you see the collapse of tourism that there is not to take a step and dirty Rome as never and we complain about (Barcelona ) for example we do not visit it is not worth it.

..

title: Colosseum: true wonder
text:
Coming to Rome and not visiting the Colosseum could be a shame.  I decided to visit it (this is the fourth time I come to Rome). The three stars are attributed solely for the cultural-historical aspect, if not for that they would have been 0.

title: Nice trip bad Award!
text: We had a tour of the Colosseum basement. Nice tour guide a little hard to understand. GetYourGuide took an unreasonable overprice!! The ticket cost us kr 1080 but can see it has only cost them 240 as the price should be. And it was exactly the same tour that could be purchased at the Colosseum. Years!

title: An incredible experience…if not for the nasty rude staff
text:
The Colosseum is something that needs to be seen in person, in order to fully appreciate.

Pretty incredible to witness this structure from the inside and outside. There is also plenty of information made available inside the experience for customers to fully appreciate the significance of this structure. A must-see in Rome.

===

While the Colosseum was an impressive feat (once you do get the tickets and come at the right time), the staff managing it was the exact opposite.

First of all,  when we first arrived, it was raining heavily, and it was physically difficult to see where the ticket office was in the heavily pouring rain. Amongst the chaos, one of the staff members at the entrance shoved us into the pre-security screening area. Assuming we needed to get our belongings screened before proceeding to buy a ticket, we completed that step. Once in, we tried to buy tickets. To our surprise, we somehow passed the point where we could buy tickets, but before the point where they scanned tickets. When we asked nearby staff how to buy tickets, instead of helping direct us, they told us we should have already had tickets, and they suddenly became hostile towards us.

Once realising we may be in the wrong place (and not being able to buy the tickets online right away), we asked if we could exit so we could find the booth to buy the tickets. One staff let us out while simultaneously accusing us of forcing our way in and cheating them. When we tried to explain what happened, they just immediately cut us off, told us to get out and ignored us. I’ve never witnessed such incredibly rude and nasty staff in Europe. Especially given the fact that it was THEM who got us in that area in the first place, and we maintained being polite to them. The staff treat the customers like scum. They could not care less. These people give Italians the bad attitude reputation that they unfortunately carry. Shame on them.

title: Parco archeologico del Colosseo

title: Wonderous!

title: very expensive tourism in Rome

title: Good tour to take - different guide or tour company (Carrani Tours)

She had no sense of humor nor did she read her audience’s at all - long explanations when clearly the group was asking for something different (the entire group!). text: No guide, promised our money back minus the entrance fee, still waiting, able to go on our own. It is probably a good tour, just not for us.

title: Basic ticket no longer allows a meaningful view of the site
text:
Unbelievably awful relative to how it used to be.

The basic ticket is now restricted to a route that actively prevents you from actually seeing the Colosseum!!!!

You used to be able to access the Colosseum floor level and appreciate the sheer scale of the stadium above you.

Now... you're bottled into a route that winds you up and around the exterior of the building, in narrow confines, being pushed and shoved through a route that has been designed to feel claustrophobic throughout and where you can't see any of the "exhibits" due to the over-crowding (most of them are filler anyway, much less impressive than the building you're being prevented from properly seeing).

At the very end of your route, you'll have a chance to fight a massive scrum of people for a chance to see the Colosseum how you used to be able to see it.

The "pay extra" tickets allow you to see what you used to get for standard price.

Essentially, elitists have taken over the building and created an experience that is far more pleasant for the rich and actively harmful to the poor.  The whole thing is now money-grubbing and plutocratic by design, but I guess the conservators have captured some of the truth of what a visit to the Colosseum would have been like for the Roman plebs - crowded, uncomfortable, and you can't see Jack Sh1t.

title: Majestic, but not for the handicapped.

On the Colosseum and the Roman Forum Palatine nothing else can be said that is majestic.

title: Excellent sight, but far too overcrowded

text: Visited the Colosseum on August 6, 2024, and it was really hot on this day. Locating our representative to get our tickets was no problem and we were actually able to get them early but could only enter 15 minutes before the scheduled time. I would suggest going during the off season if you want to enjoy it and actually be able to walk around. We spent about 25-30 minutes inside before we had enough of the crowd and exited. Remember to bring an umbrella or else you will bake in the sun.

title: Skip arena only tickets

title: date errors - no after service

title: 31st July at 9:30 AM
text:
31st July at 9:30 AM

The Colosseum remains a breathtaking historical marvel, offering a glimpse into ancient Rome's grandeur. Visiting on the 31st of July at 9:30 AM, we encountered extremely hot weather, with temperatures reaching 38°C. While the monument itself was spectacular, the experience was slightly marred by a few factors.

Firstly, the area outside the Colosseum was filled with aggressive vendors trying to sell various items, which detracted from the overall experience. Inside, despite arriving early, the site was already very crowded. We've visited before in March and found the experience more pleasant, as the crowds were smaller and the temperatures cooler. For future visits, especially with children, we recommend avoiding school holidays if possible.

The Colosseum offers minimal shade, and seating is sparse, making it challenging to escape the heat. Despite these challenges, the history and ongoing efforts to enhance the educational experience at the site are commendable. The addition of new learning opportunities and exhibits enriches each visit.

However, it should be noted that many parts of the experience now come with additional costs. From accessing the upper levels and the wooden platform to guided tours, there are many extras that weren't always in place, making the visit more expensive.

Overall, while we highly recommend visiting the Colosseum, we advise doing so outside of peak tourist seasons to avoid the crowds and heat. We rate the historical experience 4 stars, but due to the busyness and heat, the overall enjoyment was somewhat diminished. Nonetheless, it's a site worth visiting for its rich history and significance.

title: Packed to the hilt
text: Needs an overhaul for the visitor numbers .It is packed to the hilt. Needs proper shops selling drinks, ice lollies and gifts, instead it relies on men down on their luck selling water, fans and silk umbrellas. The money this attraction is making must be colossal so  employ these men in the shops, more enjoyable for the tourist and you are helping these men that are down on their luck. Tragic this money making pit is not more charitable.

title: Chaos
text:
An astounding piece of history. 
Chaotic mess getting in! 
Two separate tour guides told us it was full so we had to go with them. 
Then we realized that we could buy tickets. Long line, need ID for each {luckily we had pictures}.
Where to buy tickets, entrance etc wasn't obvious. People were not helpful at all. In fact they were rude but we found this in much of Rome. 
It could be so much better organized. 
I am glad we saw it but I wouldn't go back.

title: do not recommend
text: signed up for 12pm tour. told to arrive 15min early at tourstation office, which is a 20min walk from colosseum. It took over 20min to check in. had to pay $1 for bathroom. given 2:15pm tour time and told to "go walk around". this changed our plans for the day as we were expecting 12pm tour time. would not recommend.

title: Amazing place, Terrible experience
text:
My wife, child and myself purchased our tickets for this attraction weeks ago and we arrived around 7:45am for our 8:45am entrance time. We asked several different people about the queuing system but could not get a straight answer. we finally found the correct place to queue around 8:00am  but when 8:15 came the place was an absolute circus with no organisation at all, when the staff finally arrived they decided that the thousands of people needed to move back 4 metres which then caused more chaos. This is hands down the worst managed mayhem to a beautiful attraction I have ever witnessed. 
What made the day worse for me was when my wife. Who is physically disabled and cannot climb stairs without assistance asked to use the elevator, she was greeted with “sorry but this is only for disabled people” I am not sure if this is something which is seen across Rome but we have never been put in the position to explain ourselves before. Hidden disabilities are actually a thing. This has left a very sour taste in our mouths and I believe needs addressed and staff members better trained to handle situations like this.

title: Family trip
text: Very nice only problem that I never went into it but you can already see that it is beautiful. Very very nice from outside I love it6

title: Poorly preserved

We had the impression that we didn’t see much while culturally this place full of history is very interesting. Too bad, the organization of the "visit" is really to be reviewed in our opinion...

title: The Colosseum does not consider people with disabilities.
text: 05/22/2024 - 08:45 a.m. The place is impressive, terrible work staff. We were accompanied by a disabled person who uses a cane. title: Amazing building, poorly managed and staffed
text:

And they were going to refund the tour guide price. When we arrived we had nothing but hassle about our tickets saying that they had already been used. One lady who I was asking for help just kept turning her back on me and walking away to deal with somebody else. title: Terrible service, amazing building
text: Went through the painful process of getting our full experience tickets with the arena and undergound included, which included constantly refreshing the terrible ticket sale website. We arrived at the colosseum 15 minutes before our 9:30 am time slot as recommended. After showing our tickets at the entry we asked where to go and were pointed onwards. We continued to ask the staff we encountered along the way for guidance and were just ushered on to the next area. Eventually when we asked the attendent at the entrance to the arena, she said we needed to be with a group to go underground. We were eventually directed back to the entrance where amongst all the people and other signs there, there was a small sign saying undergound group meeting place. The guide there told us we had missed our group and that there was nothing he could do. When I asked if the two of us could just tag along with the next group, he said it was fully booked and gave us no additional form of recourse. There was no indication during the booking process, recieving the tickets, or upon entry, indicating that we would be joining a group to go to the underground, and there were no instructions given on what to do when we got there. We took every effort during the planning and execution of our visit to gather all the information to make things go smoothly, and tried utilize staff to further this. Overall it is terrible customer service and a terrible experience.  If you are going, just get a guided tour and avoid the terrible service that they have developed.

title: Enjoy
text:
We booked online directly through the colosseum, no need to book through tour companies. Unfortunately I was late booking therefore the online time I could book was 1:30. 
We arrived at the colosseum around 12:30 as unsure of the process. 

Children are free, but unable to book these in advance theeefore on arrival go through the advance booking line and once inside after security there is a ticket box and they give you the child’s ticket here…. Really simple process! 

Queues look huge but go down really quickly and we were inside within 15/20 minutes. 

This was our main reason to come to Italy alongside Pompeii however I must be in the minority but I found it quite underwhelming. The amount of tickets they sell your squashed inside, constantly being moved along, everyone pushing to get a photo opportunity we couldn’t enjoy it. 

It was nice to have visited and we got lovely photos but in all honestly the outside is the most impressive and I kind of feel I would be satisfied with visiting the outside rather than actually going in!

title: My two bullets do not refer to the monument

title: Don’t expect the workers to be friendly, nor compassionate.
text: I took my 83 year old mother and my 82 year old father for the first time from the U.S. today 5/26. I had bought our tickets online. We were so excited! We got through the line after waiting 30 minutes or so. The guy checked our tickets and let us through with a sticker. We walked a ways taking pictures. Then we got to another point, where they were checking tickets again. Unfortunately, it was my fault, but we came a day early. Our tickets were for the 27th. I said can we please just go today (since the place is an absolute zoo) plus we almost missed our time,  since taxis aren't as easy to get as they say. The lady was so callous and cold. No come back tomorrow, or purchase new tickets! The line for new tickets would take at least a hour or more to stand in line and mom can’t do that! There were hundreds upon hundreds of people there. Two more elderly people wouldn’t make a difference,  plus we had tickets, bought and paid for, but just for the next day!  I’m not sure what kind of people turn away 2 people in their 80s?We left and saw some other sites. We will return tomorrow, but unfortunately my mother will have to stay behind, since she has health issues and can’t make the journey two days in a row, plus she has to conserve her energy for the Vatican! It just broke my heart that they are more concerned with making money and following the rules, then using their common sense and compassion to allow my mom to experience what she flew all the way from America to see! Shame on you!

title: Disappointing
text: I booked a tour with Get Your Guide but apparently I managed to book a tour without a guide and I also paid for a ticket for a 17 year old which apparently is free I was very disappointed as we had no one to explain the history and we ended up on a self tour the sights were amazing but lack of a tour guide was unforgivable this company must know that the reason you book through them is to get a tour with a  guide.   What was most surprising was we had been on a tour with them  through the Vatican the day before which was excellent

title: Tripadvisor is terribly unreliable.
text:
Tripadvisor is terrible. Never book through them.
You pay double the price. In addition, she canceled our reservation the night before.
The customer service was incredibly rude and lazy.

title: Respect the tourist
text:
Nothing to say about the beauty of the Colosseum and the forums which deserve 10 stars.
The negative opinion is due to the behavior of the entrance staff.
Presumptuous and rude in general to the point of being offensive and rude if you allow yourself to negatively underline your behavior.
A similar situation has never happened.
The tourist must be respected

title: Buy tickets with a guided tour!
text: Unless you have a guided tour, it isn’t worth fighting the crowds to see the inside of the colosseum.  Even with the audio app, it wasn’t worth the effort to fight the crowds.

title: Always busy
text: The Colosseum is impressive. Getting into it is not. I was there 3 times in April 2024. You stand in line for 1 1/2 to two hours to buy a ticket. The ticket you buy may be for an hour or two later. Then you get in the entry line when it’s your time. If you want to get in with the least hassle, there are usually tour guides who’ll add you to their group for about 55 euros. Where the lines are entering there are obvious groups. Many times a guide will stand apart yet near the group. Some will likely approach you if you are close to the line. 55 euros may seem like an expensive entry, but worth it to me, and you also have a guide. The Metro stops right at the Colosseum. It is very crowded at that station. There are announcements and signs warning of pickpockets. Tour guides told me Rome tourism has no off season. Midsummer weather is hot.

title: The feeling of being cheated
text: We purchased full experience tickets on the official website for 5:15 p.m. We went to the meeting point for the basement tour at 5:10 p.m. and about ten people were waiting with us. Around 5:45 p.m., someone came to us to tell us that we wouldn't be able to go down to the basement because we weren't at the meeting point at 5:15 p.m., which is not true. Despite argument, we were unable to visit the basement. We felt like we were being cheated. The visit was still interesting, but we really wanted the basement. Too bad, because it leaves a bitter taste...

title: Dissatisfied
text: The tour as well as another tour through trip advisor was canceled at the last minute. When one travels as far as I did for these tours and then can’t get another one can ruin a trip.

title: Be careful with online reservations
text:
To have ! But apart from the Easter holiday crowds!
Avoid so-called “skip the line” tickets from agencies like “head out”: a great scam! On site, tickets are free for young people under 18 and cost €18 per adult: know before taking tickets online via an agency..,

title: Atrocious disappointment
text:
Purchased skip-the-line ticket. When we arrived in front of the Colosseum, we couldn't enter because the tickets were sold out.
????
Like other families.
Fraud?

title: Exceptional site but poor organization and expired audio guide…
text:
The site is exceptional. Nothing to say, we'll be amazed inside.
But a few negative points all the same: no information on having to present your ID, no information on what time to show up. Some sites tell you 30 minutes before and when you arrive, 1 in 2 people are turned away. It's true that it's complicated to put a sign at the entrance to one of the most visited sites in the world... for your information, it's 10 minutes before so there's no point in coming before...
Lousy audio guide. Old iPod from the 2000s, this could use an update. Once again, it must lack resources with 3000 people per hour…
Take a guided tour early in the morning and there you will really live the experience to the fullest!!

title: Bit of a disappointment and be careful with tickets!
text:
