Quite disappointing and overall, I regret not going back to Ephesus instead (which to me is a far better experience and has lots more to see, preserved in a better state). 

We entered via the Forum entrance at 9am in the morning (which was great as it was very quiet and we hardly had to waste time queuing). The very nice lady gave us our tickets and pointed to the 10am on it and said that’s when the colosseum would open. I asked if we had to be there for that time or if we could go in any time after that and she relaxedly said the latter. 

We enjoyed strolling through the Forum and pretty gardens until 11 and then went to enter the colosseum itself. We were abruptly told we had missed our time and when I explained why, I was told to speak with someone else…3 unsympathetic people later and I was starting to get a bit deflated and frustrated. I finally got to speak with someone at the ticket office and explained and she stated it was impossible for us to have been told that (which made me cross as I wouldn’t lie) and that we needed to pay again. I suggested perhaps I could feedback that it hadn’t been clear at all and signs around the ticket offices would be helpful to ensure people fully understand, irrespective of what someone verbally tells them (as there may be language misunderstandings etc) and she said that was no good, they’d heard it loads of times before (so it clearly wasn’t impossible to have been told that AND they have chosen not to make it clearer) and I shouldn’t feedback to her and I could email the park (I haven’t been able to find an email since being back). 

We ended up paying again as we had come all the way and it would be stupid to go home without seeing the colosseum (though to be honest, I was quite unimpressed by it compared to other places and very put off by the handling of the staff). 

All in all, really wasn’t worth it for us (though the wisteria were very pretty in the gardens).

title: Crowded and Staff Not Helpful
text: We booked a full access ticket a month ahead on the Coliseum’s very unfriendly website.  It was difficult to navigate and to operate.  When we arrived the signage was limited and the staff was tired and frustrated and did not give guidance.  Once inside the Coliseum it was difficult to navigate and figure out how to get from space to space.  I’m not sure that we were able to see all the things our full access ticket provided us.  We did use an audio tour we downloaded that helped some.  The staff inside did not seem willing to answer questions. Some signage explaining what we were seeing would have been helpful

title: Beware of “tour” operators
text:
Beware of the tour guides that approach you on the street. I’m sure some may be ok but we paid 20 euro each for 2 adults 2 children with the promise of a guided tour if coliseum and Palatine forum. 
Seemed professional with head sets so tour guide can be heard as she walked ahead. 

Took us to ticket booth where we waited 45 minutes in line to buy our own tickets. Eventually entered the coliseum where the “tour” went for 15 minutes and she said “ok tour is over now hand back your head sets and you can explore the Paletine yourself” 

The “tour” literally was 15 minutes. 

Italian government not really helping tourists by hiding the ticket booth well away from the coliseum and no signs to find it. Either book a month ahead online or do some research where the ticket booth is hidden. Trust me it’s well hidden.

title: Visit ruined - no pun intended
text: Colosseum is great, but did not have a good experience with the ticketing. My daughter is a student and so we had bought a student ticket. However we were turned away at the entrance as we are in the UK. This is apparently only for EU students. Had to buy a new ticket and was not refunded for the one already bought. Also bring your own toilet paper. No paper in any of the toilets at Palatine Hill. Disgusting!🤢

title: Awful people working gate with no understanding. Turned us away and then wouldn’t let us in. No care for customers.
text:
Showed up. Told leave. Came back. Wasn’t let in. Staff not understanding. no excuse for this poor management. 

Basically. Guy at gate said we didn’t have ticket. Sent us away to get tickets. Turns out we had them all along.  Then came back and they wouldn’t let us in because our entrance window had passed even though they turned us away at the right time. Travel all the way to Italy and almost didn’t get to see this the colosseum. Gate man and woman had zero care in the world for us our situation. Offered no resolution. 

Apparently current management is known to be terrible and is about to be replaced.

From my perspective this should have happened yesterday. 

Had to pay a huge fee to do a tour because no other tickets available this busy week. 

Quite unacceptable. Beware if you go. And don’t be late!  People who work there do not care at all. 

Hopefully new management is better. 
Can’t be worse.

title: Scammers around the coliseum don't get caught
text:
There are a number of scamers around the coliseum that offer you a way to jump the queues and include a guided tour as part of the deal. It's a scam that the authorities do nothing to counter.
You pay your money then get to stand in the same queue as everyone else to buy tickets to get in, then you stand in the same queue as everyone else to get it. Don't get caught!
Also why do they need my ID to sell me a ticket to look at a pile of rubble. It's an in invasion of privacy!
Thank God I never threw a coin into the Trevi fountain otherwise I'd have to come back

title: Let's squeeze the tourist to the maximum in Rome
text:
Like all of Rome, it is something incredible and beautiful. But the need to squeeze tourists economically overshadows it.

If you obtained the deposit a month before through the internet and you are very happy about the visit, I only tell you to think about every step you take, because they don't let you go back later. Surely you think that due to the quick "sold out" the flow of people will be controlled, well no, they get as many people as possible, the important thing is to earn as much money as possible, the same with the visit, do you want to go to the arena? Another price. Do you want to go up to the attic? Another price. Do you want to go to the underground? Another price. Did you eat beans and are you having flatulence? 1 euro for each fart.

title: Toilet Alert
text:
It’s a must see and, as you would expect, it is very busy. 
Very few toilet facilities in the immediate vicinity and the very limited ones inside are always busy and also pretty grim!

title: A moment of history
text: the Colosseum is worth seeing for its history but once inside a little disappointed very little renovated earlier consolidated by concrete and crowded with people with limited access. On the other hand, Montpalatin and its gardens are a pleasant time to do.

title: Well worth the visit
text: We booked a tour, but the guide didn't take into account anyone with disabilities so we struggled to keep up with him. We ended the tour with him 1 hour before the end and looked round ourselves. He didn't give us chance to look at points of interest  he just talked then carried on walking. Very disappointed but the place itself is amazing

title: This guide needs to take a breath.
text: An iconic place to see. Our guide talked too fast, walked too fast, did not check when the group got separated from her. Some of us could not understand her English. Overwhelmed with the amount of information that was given at such a frantic pace.

title: NOT THAT EXCITING AND NO TOILETS IN THE ENTIRE PLACE
text: Not exactly that exciting. No washrooms in the entire place. How is it possible an international tourist attraction has no toilets.

title: A little overrated
text: Just a bunch of remains, looks nice on the outside, inside loads of people, nothing much to see. You need to spend at least £70 per person to walk around all areas. This is a rip-off to be fair

title: Very busy, lots of big groups and no room to appreciate it
text: I believe we got unlucky in our timing but our trip to the Colosseum was ruined by huge groups of students and other tour groups, who kept blocking the entrances and the display of information and history of the Colosseum. We tried our best to navigate around them but it felt like the place was above capacity and we could barely move. Everyone we encountered was either oblivious or rude. Soured the experience for us and we actually couldn't wait to leave, which is sad (our time slot was 2.30pm on a Monday). One good tip we were given was to do the Forum/Palentine Hill the following day and to use the other gated entrance which is less busy. The tip paid off as the main queue for the Forum was massive and we pretty much walked in at the other smaller entrance.

title: Don't forget photo I.D is you want to go inside the Coloseum.
text:
Amazing building from the outside.
Sadly we weren't able to buy tickets after standing in the queue for 40 minutes to be told that we needed photo I.D.
There were no signs up that we could see saying that you needed I.D and no staff explaining this to everyone.
Just wanted to make sure future visitors don't turn up without I.D.

title: OK
text:
The truth is a bit disappointing
Very busy with people
There is nothing really different or impressive about the place whether you see it from the outside or go inside.
A mandatory site is true but not something that is wow in my eyes

title: False Advertised Headout & Show Me Italy Tour - no ARENA FLOOR ACCESS to Colosseum even we paid for it.
text:
Do not book your tour with Headout "Colosseum, Roman Forum, & Palatine Hill Guided Tour with Arena Floor Access." We paid Headout for the event and the touring company is "Show Me Italy".  We paid and booked this tour in advance and we never get to see the Arena Floor.   The only reason we booked this, is because the title stated "ARENA FLOOR ACCESS" It was one of the highlights we look forward to our five-year planned trip to Italy.   When checking in with the tour guide, he said he didn't receive a ticket to the arena access then took us to a view point to look down at the arena and said this is the best spot and took off.  

I demanded an answer and waited over a week still had no answer from Headout.  There are a few people from our group asking as well,  I hope they will see my post and add their complaints/experiences to mine.  Thank you for your time.

title: A blurry beauty
text:
A monument seen and reviewed from all possible angles, but which when I go back to see it in person always seems too suffocated.
Undoubtedly a stop not to be missed for anyone in Rome, but its beauty at times seems a little blurred and commodified by tourism

title: Too crowded and unorganized
text:
Right now it seems that their business is in the guided tours (€41 pp), if you want the tickets buy them online (€18 pp), if you decide to buy them there it may take more than 2 hours to get it at the ticket office.
On the other hand, the organization is non-existent, everyone is sent to the same place despite there being other alternatives, so the crowds that form inside are shameful, since the recommended capacity is far exceeded.

If you want to enjoy the experience, it is best to go first thing in the morning.

The most beautiful and interesting thing is to see it from the outside.

title: SCAM DO NOT USE
text: AWFUL. do not use this website. It is a scam. We were denied entry at the colosseum even though we had paid for the all access ticket. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. I was left very upset. The ticket agents scanned my tickets and then denied my entry so they are claiming that the tickets were used even though we were not allowed in unless another ticket was bought.

title: Run down almost like left to ruin
text:
Was a lot more broken than i thought it would be, at £15 a pop you'd think they'd invest in repairing it. Untidy.
Don't recognise it from Gladiator or Enter the Dragon.
Lots of Senegalese outside selling tat.
Harder to get through than an airport.

title: Arrogant and rude personnel
text: Colloseum as such is nice and interesting, but personnel, staff, security etc. are extremely arrogant  and not service minded at all! They are there for the visitors and not the other way round. Many of them should find another job.

title: Disrespect for tourists
text: I purchased a guided tour of the underground for myself, my wife and my ten year old son. I arrived at the meeting point on time and the employee who helped me left us waiting. I lost the group and I had to run after them. But the worst part was entering the Roman forum. Total disorganization in the queue, with groups accompanied by guides jumping the queue all the time. And the Coop employees are condescending about it. After at least 30 people passed by, I didn't accept another group and went in. The employee started yelling at me, and a security guard came and took me out, along with my crying son and my wife. They told me to go to the end of the line. I justified it, I apologized for the stress, but they continued to treat me badly. I bought the ticket on the official website and felt completely disrespected. About 4 employees treated me very badly, harshly and shouting, in front of my son and wife. The visit is interesting, but the company should be aware of this disrespect.

title: Becareful you go the right way and not get overwhelmed by the crowds
text: It is interesting to see the architecture but tbh even in off season it was absolutely heaving. If you are not in a tour prepared to be bombarded by the tour guides and the mindless sheep following them and bumping into you. We ended up going the wrong way and missed half the tour and suddenly was at the exit. As we walked past the exhibition we went down the stairs when we should’ve went left. When we told the attendant this at first she said that’s unfortunate but it is one way. I wasn’t having this and spoke to someone on the exit who was shocked to hear this and sent us back saying to look for someone in yellow jacket. They weren’t them but only staff we could get to. I challenged her again as I wasn’t missing half of what we paid for. It was apparent that while we were there at least 2 other groups done the same. we were able to go back round I think only because we said we missed the arena (which you pay extra for). I said to her clearly this happens a lot and she said yes! I imagine this has all happened since they have privatised and got external services to operate it charging a lot to enter and stuff you full of people. There should definitely be better signage/ block off the way we went so it is one way.

title: Kulture turned turist attraction.
text: We where here out of season and to think this placed is designed to house thousands of people it felt very crowded at the architectual design is totally ruined by the museum installation. Do NOT bother with the audioguide - watch a YouTube video before visiting instead. But it is still impressive. Go to Roman Forum while you are here anyways!

title: Mandatory visit, but be patient
text: A must-see historical site, but I found the visit unorganized and tumultuous. Of course the place is incredible, but the queues, disorganized direction of the visit and little access to interesting places made the visit to the Colosseum the least interesting of my stay in Rome. Even though we chose the Full Experience visit, we only had access to a 'mezzanine' above the basement (with a great view, without which the experience would have been even worse). The flow of people is poorly managed, with little circulation space, and the information is not clear.

title: Must
text: A must fun and a must if you go to Rome, but go with single tickets, takes too much time if you go in a group......etc etc ............... .....

title: Waste of time
text: Like being cattle herded to market. Wish we’d just looked at it from the outside to be honest. There was not much to see inside and it was a faff getting in and out again.

title: Shambolic procedure
text: A fantastic place. Ruined by complete disorganisation. You get there with no signs or information of what to do. People harassing you to join there tour parties for fast track entrance. We joined one at 20 euros per person still took 2 hours to get in. There are no toilets outside except in information centre and only one inside. We went on the first Sunday of the month which is free entry. Might be worth getting ticket on line beforehand. Once in well worth a visit. As usual many people trying to sell you stuff.

title: Filthy dirty entrance
text:
Absolutely stunning place, it was so beautiful anytime of the day.
Limited opening times in the winter.
Very reasonable prices.
As with the rest of Rome city.
Is being neglected. Could believe the state of the place.
Probably Europes dirtiest cities.
Was disgusting. A lot of the cities architecture is being neglected.

title: Great wonder, it's a shame she's Italian.
text: Very bad organization when entering. There are no tours in Spanish. Too many very funny African vendors, they don't even respect the person, they physically attacked me and the police don't even notice. The coliseum always under reconstruction. It is very sad that a work considered a wonder of the world is not organized at the entrance, it is surrounded by thugs and many street vendors. There are no signs and the native people are very rude to tourists no matter where you come from.

title: Step into a piece of history.
text:
There have been a few changes to the Colosseum since was last there 13 years ago. There are many displays of artifacts and models that are worth seeing. There is also the option to go onto a platform onto the arena. There have also been many improvements to make it more  accessible to less mobile or disabled people, such as ramps and elevators (Which do not affect the appearance.)

What really lets the Colosseum down is selfish tour guides who take up the vantage points for long periods of time lecturing their groups, meaning others can't get in to take photos. Tour group leaders also need to ask their groups to only take up 1/2 of a path or walkway.

A visit to the Colosseum is a must when visiting Rome. A bit of advice - DO NOT purchase anything from touts or people walking up to you trying to sell you things as they are not licensed sellers or even residents of Italy. Book any tours either directly through the Colosseum, or through a licenced tour operator.

title: Honestly, I expected better
text: From the outside it is wonderful, but from the inside it gave me mixed emotions. The grandeur of the work is undoubted, but a great deal of imagination is needed to visually reconstruct what it contained. There are truly better preserved amphitheaters in even unknown places.

title: The place is amazing
text: Don't get suckered in by the people with official tourist guide ID cards, smartly dressed. We did but thankfully got all our money back. Just go and get a ticket and look round,it's an amazing place, spoilt by the scammers.

title: Pick up place for tickets shut.
text:
I booked a Skip the line Coleseum Roman Forum and Pallentine Hill entrance ticket. 
We had to collect tickets from an address near the colleseum before our entrance time 10:00. We arrived early- the building was closed. We returned at 20 mins to our entrance time ( the place was about 10-15 mins walk away) still no one at the building. I then had to call the Ancient Roman Tours office at my expense on  a foreign phone.  Once I spoke to someone he texted my tickets through- not sure why they couldn’t have done this to start with and save us a journey. 
Other than this our trip was fantastic. We got audio guides at €6 each and spent over 5 hours wandering around all 3 venues. It’s a pity it started in a stressful way .

title: A nameless brothel
text:
Aaaah the Italian organization... a world... but a world... what's the point of making time slots if it's to be all on top of each other like sardines in a box that's too narrow.
A happy mess made up of screams and selfies, groups of 50 bewildered plebeians with no autonomy of their own blocking the corridors, stopping at the top of a staircase to take photos even if it meant blocking any exit… a mess… but a mess… we ended up leaving in order to return at another probably calmer period to savor this place which undoubtedly deserves a little more tranquility. When will we recruit intelligent personnel in Italy capable of understanding that making figures is good but making sure not to make each visit a permanent nightmare is better?

title: NICE CITY, BUT BEWARE
text:
ROME is a beautiful city with all the ancient architecture  you will love.
HOWEVER,,,,1. MANY NORTH AFRICANS SCAMMERS TRYING TO SELL YOU STUFF 
LIKE CRAPY BRACELETS AND THEY ARE VERY AGGRESIVE. 2. PEOPLE TRYING TO 
HELP YOU AT METRO STATION THEN TRY TO SCAM MONEY OUT OF YOU. 
3. MOST TAXI'S ARE GREAT,FAIR AND HONEST. BUT,,BUT  THERE ARE A FEW SCAMMERS.

title: Mandatory stop
text: Impossible to go to Rome and not visit the Colosseum. That said, I preferred to admire it from outside, from the Palatine, and in the evening with its fascinating lighting.

title: Not as expected
text:
Got sucked in by the people doing tours, expensive for what it was. 
Very modernised and had construction going on at the time.
Don't go when weather is wet as no shelter!
More exciting on the outside.

title: Pay attention to local agencies
text:
Not to mention visiting the places which are simply magnificent.
We had previously reserved our entry tickets via the tripadvisor platform and the ARTOUR agency. It was specified to collect the tickets 30 minutes before the visit from the agency, however the agency being closed we were not able to collect them the same day, which forced us to pay again for a full price entry ticket. The agency does not answer the phone and no email address is mentioned. I therefore recommend that you buy your tickets on site which are €17 per person (without guide obviously) and for the Colosseum/Palatine/Forum. The tickets are supposedly “non-refundable” but I find this unacceptable in our case.

title: It is a must visit point
text: It is a must experience; however, be ready to walk uneven stairs. If you need a bathroom use it in the beginning of your tour. Follow pics and explanations because they are helpful.

title: Very bad, I don't recommend it
text:
Rude and lazy staff, 5 minutes late, they left us out with rudeness and insistence
P.s. we are a school group, I don't recommend going to Milan

title: Don't pay rip-off prices.
text: You have to see it if you visit Rome but it is a huge tourist rip-off. If you want to get inside you have to either book weeks in advance, join a 3-hour queue - which moves at snails' pace - on the day or pay exorbitant prices to one of dozens of tour guides who have been allowed to buy tickets in advance so that there are few left for sale directly to visitors. The tourist office have clearly become aware of this disgrace and have just decided to make more tickets available on the day, but really need to address the scandal of resale of tickets. You actually get a pretty good idea of how amazing the place is just by walking the whole way round outside. Then spend the hours that you saved not queueing by going to the Baths of Caracalla (just as amazing and almost empty) or the Baths of Diocletian for huge, awe-inspiring  Roman architecture.

title: Colossuem
text:
Staff Friendly, smooth entry, so glad we booked inadvance and had skip the line tickets. 
Paid extra for an audio guide which was very informative.
Not rushed to move through but better signage / one way system would have been helpful.
Toilets awful, doors broken, missing toilet seats, soap dispensers and water not working - bit of a theme with toilet facilities we found in Rome.

title: crumbling and old.
text: Much ado about nothing. not even got a roof? when they finising it. needs a bit of maintenance, seems to be parts missing.

title: Unfriendly reception at the entrance
text:
The tour of the Colosseum was 
impressive, but the joy of it was significantly dampened when we entered: an extremely unfriendly guard at the entrance, a mafioso type, refused entry to all visitors and sent them back with harsh words, even though the tickets said that you should arrive 10 minutes early.

title: Waste of my visit to colloseum
text: We never visited the Colosseum as the ticket deliverer never turned up. We phoned the deliverer and never answered the call. So we missed once in a lifetime visit to the Colosseum  took this up with Tripadviser and till today nobody came back to me

title: Total disappointment
text: Disappointing. 3 hours waiting time. All tickets sold out online 1 month in advance. Ticket Mafia buys everything in advance to sell on site for €69 for groups and skip the line (instead of the €18 standard price). I was so excited to visit the Colosseum at first, but after everything I lost all joy. Absolutely not worth it. 0 points

title: Not Colossale enough!
text: My experience of il Colosseo was probably a bit better than “average” but clearly a full rung below “very good”. For a stadium that’s nearly 2,100 years-old and has had all the wear and (in some cases deliberate) tear it’s had to endure over those millennia, it’s survival, partially intact at least,  is impressive. But maybe I’ve just got this Hollywood “sword and sandals” image fixed in my head thanks to Spartacus, Gladiator and countless other Colosseumesque flicks, but I was expecting an arena of that stature to be much larger and grander in scope and size.  A field day for archaeologists and historically massicciamente significativo I’m sure, but I was left feeling a little underwhelmed.

title: Book tickets!
text:
We enjoyed our visit and it is a marvellous building.  The explanation displays are clear.  It was very crowded but worth spending time to see it.  
Our standard ticket did not include the basement area, where they kept the animals etc.  This was only accessible with a booked tour which was disappointing.

It is really good that the ticket was a joint one with entrance to the Forum and Palatine hill in a 24 hour period, so we were able to access that area the following day.

title: City of Wonders Rome Tour Cancelled at the Last Minute
text: Trip planners BEWARE.  I booked a private tour of the Colosseum/Palatine Hill for my family of 7 back in March 2023 for close to $1000 with City of Wonders - 7 months before our trip.  These companies make you pay in full at the time of booking.  Last weekend was our scheduled tour and 10 minutes before it was to start, their customer service line in Ireland called my cell phone to cancel the tour!!!  These companies are getting too large and really do not have contingency plans in place when they make mistakes.  People like us travel from all over the world and make plans.  Cancelling at the last minute ruins the trip and these companies really don't care.  My recommendation is to hire a tour company that will give you your guides contact information from the very beginning so you stay in contact with them as your trip gets closer.  With these large companies, you are just a number and not important.  City of Wonders Promise is "Our team is dedicated to making sure every experience is a great one."  Well that can't be farther from the truth.  Thank you for ruining our Rome weekend.

title: Very bad - not recommended!!
text: The tickets were ridiculously expensive - the service was poor: we got the tickets and had to queue twice! Once for the ticket from Tripadvisor and then for the ticket for our son, which would have been free if we hadn't booked through this platform! In addition, it was no longer possible to visit the Roman Forum that day! But we left the next day! We should have been informed of this! For that price: zero service!

title: 'the veil of strange verses'" Dante (Inf IX 63)
text:
From a scientific point of view, everything has been said about the Colosseum, or at least it is believed that everything has been said. In reality it is one of those iconic monuments, where the archaeological investigation, the restoration, the statics of the monument are subordinate to the use of mass tourism.
It is today understood with an 'industrial' and speculative approach, where what is contrary to the 'formulas' of the valorisation of current cultural heritage is a 'stumbling block'. Who has ears to hear....

title: Don’t Use Dream Tourism! A Nightmare!
text: Dream Tourism realty let us down on this. We were to receive our tickets 24 hours in advance which were prepaid. We got nothing. Twelve hours before the tour I called TripAdvisor to tell them I got nothing. After they contacted Dream Tourism they and I were told the tickets were going out at 11:30pm and 12:00am that night. When I woke at 6:50am the next morning I had no tickets. I contacted Dream Tourism on the listed phone number and was told to email them my TripAdvisor voucher through WhatsApp.  When I ask how to contact them through it they hung up. I called TripAdvisor who worked with me 3 hours before our tour was booked to get my tickets. TripAdvisor was patient and stayed on the line to figure out what was the proper contact info for Dream Tourism in WhatsApp. I was able to send in my voucher to which I received tickets 1.5 hours before my tour. When I got to the Colosseum it was not the original tickets I ordered. Dream Tourism sent me a WhatsApp message they will refund me the full amount of the tickets. I’d give them a zero rating if I could. Waiting to see if I get a refund or if I need to contest through my credit card.

title: Meh.
text: Yes, there it is. So not amazing. One gets more from photographs. Entirely not worth the effort to schedule tickets, wait in line, and tour the thing.

title: Drifting area. I ask for more cleaning, more checks. For the rest he has a lot to tell. Let's take care of history
text: We have to take care of places like the Colosseum. It's filthy, dirty and they absolutely must take action.

title: It's not worth waiting in line.
text: It is more beautiful on the outside than on the inside, if you are not interested in hiring a guide to explain the history to you, it is not worth waiting in line for 3-4 hours. Because they only have 5 people selling tickets. Chaos really!! And if you have the Roma Pass you have to have booked months in advance otherwise you will have to wait in line 😅. The forum and palatines are a lot to walk around! You can also see it from the street and it is the same! And like everything in Rome full of people!

title: GetYourGuide….avoid booking with this company!!!
text:
Avoid booking through this company at all costs, unless you want to be disappointed!! I booked in advance tickets for the Colosseum tour for my dads birthday with my family, we flew to Rome specifically for this trip, only to be told a few hours before the tour that it had been cancelled, due to a “political event” which didn’t happen or interrupt any of the tours going on, despite us seeing groups from the same company going straight into the venue in front of us. 
Customer service were rubbish and unhelpful, and gave us no alternative or option for us to attempt to turn round this already awful disappointing day. All I received was an email to say the tour had been cancelled with no actual reason. Shocking, you put faith into these companies (and pay extra for the service) to guarantee bookings, and to be told it has been cancelled with no actual reason is completely unacceptable, and has ruined our family trip to Rome!!!

title: No communication so it didn’t happen
text: I booked the tour on my phone the night before. The tour said it would pick up at your hotel. When I entered my hotel, it didn’t show up. I guess it wasn’t on their pick up site list. But they never gave a list. I tried to contact them via the “Contact Tour Operator” messaging on the Trip Advisor website to ask them where to meet a couple times before the tour time. I also called their contact phone number and left a voicemail message with my phone number. I went to the Colosseum in hopes that they would tell me where I could meet the group. They did not contact me at any point. I asked for a refund in the Contact Tour Operator messaging and still haven’t received communication from them. A list of pick up points or ANY communication would have been helpful.

title: Do not use Tiqets or Omnia if you visit Colosseum
text: Do not book with Tiqets or Omnia. They changed the time multiple times a day before my scheduled time and I never got to see the Colosseum or a refund. Several others in my tour had a similar experience. I'm sure the Colosseum is amazing from the inside, but the ticketing situation is a travesty.

title: guided tour ruined by the behavior of the guards inside the Colosseum
text: the Colosseum is magnificent. shame about the security service inside, rude and unprofessional. closing at 7.00pm and 6.30pm they practically started pushing us out. they escorted us to the exit in barbaric ways, as if we were slaves in the times of the Roman Empire. shame, excellent guided tour ruined by their behavior.

title: Disappointment
text: Well, I was a little disappointed with the Coliseum. The first time I went I couldn't get in and I was sad so on the last day of the trip I had an empty seat I managed to go so I didn't get a seat, the line was quite long and we went very early in the morning before the ticket office even opened. Okay, we got used to the queues in Rome more or less, but after cutting the ticket I waited another two hours in line because we had to get in at the time the ticket was written. When we managed and entered I was disappointed I expected more imposing more beautiful, I don't know....

title: Nice if you can get tickets
text:
Yes of course you should go! It is incredible to be standing in it. 
My problem is with how to get in it.
Tickets come on sale a month in advance and get snatched by bots. The only way to get in is to be a bot or to buy the tickets via a third party tour operator for an exorbitant amount of money. 
The different types of tickets make no sense. Don't count on the Colosseum website to clarify things, or I am too stupid to understand it, but it doesn't matter anyway because you can't buy tickets via the website cause they are getting bought by bots!
There is also one toilet in the whole Colosseum and it's at the beginning so don't miss your chance! 
There is a serious lack of explanation about anything. But why are you complaining? You should have listened in history in elementary school! 
It was very hard to find out what objects were allowed to be brought in, only to have accidentally brought one without issue. Good thing I didn't plan on lighting fires with my deodorant!
So overall yes it is amazing. The search for tickets not so much.

title: Book in advance or you might not get in....
text:
I've given this only 2 stars as we actually didn't get to go in....the queue was about 3 hours long and when we got to the front they had sold out of tickets so we couldn't go in. 
Book in advance and you'll be fine!!

title: Good guide, overbooked
text: Good tour of colosseum and palatine hill. Unfortunately the group was overbooked and made the experience much less personal. Valentina, our guide, was personable and informative. Difficult to manage so many people.

title: 150 Meter Line to Buy Tickets - READ REVIEW SO YOU KNOW HOW TO PLAN AHEAD
text: PLEASE READ SO YOU CAN PLAN AHEAD:   Buy your tickets for the Colosseum ONLINE weeks before you arrive in Rome.  Otherwise, you will stand outside in the rain, sleet, snow, sun, heat, wind and weather for HOURS and HOURS just to get a ticket to get inside.  There is usually only 1 single person at the ticket office selling tickets.  There are no covered areas to stand under and be out of the elements.  We tried standing in line for about 1 hour with horrible heat and sun, until we finally just gave up.   All we got were photos of the outsides.  There are tour groups offering a way to skip the lines.  Some are real and cost more than a regular ticket, but worth it.  But some are scams so be careful.  Keep your valuables in a safe at the hotel or leave at home.  Hold on to everything and zippered pockets are the best for pants as they have more protection.  Lots of bottled water being sold in the area and you will need it.  One (1) Euro is the going price and that is very fair for cold water.

title: Beware of CoopCulture Official Coliseum Site.
text: I bought the tickets directly from the official ticket seller, called CoopCulture. The purchase went through my credit card and I received an authorization from unicredit but no confirming email. I sent in a request for tickets and help form 4 times. Never received a reply. I checked both email and spam folders constantly. I saw several complaints about this on other sites. We are going directly to the ticket office tomorrow an hour in advance of our entry time and hoping we get in. Buyer beware! (I had better luck with non-official vendors for the Parthenon visit this morning). CoopCulture—where is your phone help?

title: Worth a visit once
text: You feel small in this huge building, we had warm but cloudy weather, which we were grateful for. Buy guided tours through registered companies not from those who go around trying to sell to those standing in long queues... for us it took about 2 hours to get inside the gates which is completely normal if you don't buy guided tours. If there's nothing good to eat and drink when you're there, sort it out beforehand

title: Unimpressed, but a must do
text:
Is it amazing to see its architecture from afar? Yes. Is it cool to follow the steps of history? Definitely. Is it mind blowing to see the ruins of the marvel? Not really. 

I wasn’t expecting to love this place originally bit I still left underwhelmed. There are only a few spaces that are preserved enough to transport you to another time and exhibits are mot the greatest if you are not with a guided tour. 

Be aware of this but go to appreciate how humanity has been capable of amazing and horrible things for a long, long time.

title: Viator - Avoid
text:
We were booked at 4.30pm due to our train coming into Rome at 3pm. However, our train was late which had a knock on effect to getting to hotel and the meeting point of the tour.

We were on our way and the guide called me at 4.15pm which is the first contact I’d had. I explained we are running about 10 mins past the start time and she said it was ok but send my location so she could track me which I did. Messaged again at just before 4.30pm to advise we’re 4 mins away and then called when we arrived. No-one was there so I called the guide and she said they went and started. At no point did the guide say they needed to start before.

I understand the voucher says arrive 30 mins before start time but it’s not that obvious and I had to look a bit harder for it.

No refund is being issued, not even partial.

title: Training of employees in dealing with disabled people is recommended!
text: Interesting sight. The necessary infrastructure for disabled and chronically ill people to visit is also available. The staff working at these facilities should be trained. When the relevant entrance ticket is shown, which has already been checked at the cash desk for eligibility, it is inappropriate to look up and down and back to see what is wrong with the person. There are also illnesses that are not immediately apparent to outsiders. This annoyed us throughout the entire visit. Instead of taking the elevator, we took the steep stairs.

title: Worst service in the tourist sector
text:
I don't understand what kind of employees who work in the tourism sector not only give wrong directions (my colleague and I had already bought the ticket but they sent us to the queue anyway and when they realized the mistake, they didn't even apologize ) and do not know how to speak English, this being the universal language, nor do they make the slightest effort to try to understand it.

A shame! I don't intend to go back.

title: Very poor experience and will never use them again
text: Booked, confirmed and paid for a sunset tour of the colosseum.  The guide did not show at the appointment tour time and we were 35 minutes early. After a phone call and on line,chat with ‘Get your guide” I was told the tour was reschedule to 45 minutes earlier.  I was sent supposedly sent an email which I never received nor did they attempt to reach me by phone.  We obviously missed the tour and not only that they would not issued a refund because they said did not cancel in the required time even though they rescheduled the tour, ridiculous. Adding insult to injury it was then too late to buy non guided tour tickets. Do not trust them. Very poor customer service.  I will be stopping payment on my credit card.

title: Do Not Book with Colosseum Tours!!
text: We booked our tour online through Colosseum Tours. They sent us a confirmation and directed us where to meet our guide for an 8:30 pm tour. We arrived early at the meeting spot but no one from Gemini Tours (who we were supposed to meet) was there. Other tour groups came to the meeting spot and assured us we were in the right place, but still no one came. We tried to call the company and got voicemail several times. We emailed the company but got no response. Finally a guide from another group was able to get in touch with a guide from Gemini Tours on his phone. She said she had no record of our reservation for that day (or any other day). We received an email the next morning with a refund but no apology or explanation of what happened. Very disappointed not to see the Colosseum on what would have been a great final night in Rome.

title: Roman Coliseum
text: Majestic!!! An unmissable visit. Congratulations to the municipality of Rome for the level of maintenance and conservation of all these works

title: If you don't think the Roman Forum is a version of pizza, you don't need this tour guide. An audio guide would have been better.
text: German-speaking guided tour of the Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine for €55. Very superficial, little content, difficult to understand German, tour guide was very small and did not have the usual ability to recognize people, so she often disappeared in the crowd and we wasted some time trying to find the woman again. Rome was supposedly founded in 700 BC.

title: Colosseo, Rome Italy
text:
The history behind the structure of this Amphitheater is marked by a significant value to the present day in Rome. Seeing it up close is an accomplishment on a traveler's bucket list. 

The weather was so high on the day of my visit (27 JUL 2023) that you couldn't really appreciate the whole place. However, it is remarkable to see it and learn how people appreciate the tourism system, given the amount of tourists around Rome and other nearby Italian cities.

title: Mucho precio, poca accesibilidad
text: Poco para el precio. Hay que reservar con tiempo y la verdad es majestuoso, pero podría estar mucho más acondicionado, pero claro, para qué si siempre lo tienen petao.

title: Visit yourself without a guide. You can use the official audio option
text: Queue was a little long so we chose to pay a guide to skip the main queue. Didn't have to wait too long however guide raced around and was not very informative. 50 euro each for ticket. We would have been better waiting in the queue and taken the official audio option. Guides are just eager to do as many groups as they can. But of a conveyor belt. I'd advise to just buy tickets from the main ticket office.

title: Pretty unorganised online ticket redemption system
text: The rating is not for the building.. of course this is amazing if not a little unloved ( visit the amphitheatre in Pula Croatia if you want to see one that has been much better looked after).. of course walking in the footsteps of gladiators is too amazing for words.. what was hard was that all the pre booked tickets needed to be collected way too far away from the attraction.. and seriously you must prebook if you are travelling in summer….  we then had to go to another office to redeem a child ticket, then walk to the Colloseum in blazing sun.. I get that Rome is hot but why wouldn’t you have the office at the railway station? Across the road from everything.. or set it up together with the ticket office ? Just spoilt the experience. Maybe book a small group tour to avoid the run around

title: Disappointing
text:
Waited over 90 minutes in shadeless scorching heat to purchase tickets. My wife was waiting under a clump of trees to avail of some shade. A policeman asked her to move away from under the trees…..to where? To burn in the shadeless open heatwave? Very stupid policeman!!
I don’t understand which donkey decided to move the ticket purchasing (and queue) to the exposed outside instead of utilizing the existing sales windows within the shaded lower corridors of the Coliseum? He/she needs electric shock treatment to reactivate the brain.
Coliseum visit was very disappointing. The ruins have been repaired without any thought….just by using concrete…,without even a try for maintaining aesthetics.
The only good part of the visit were the various water spouts which provided cold clean water.

title: Gateway to hell, unpleasant
text:
Oh dear. What a disappointment.

Be Aware!

- Don't listen to the indian "gentlemens" strolling the square in front of the Colosseum. They will offer you skip the line pass and rip you off without getting access to actual site.

- Buy only from ticket office or in advance from internet! NEVER TRUST fast offers on site!

- Ticket line is 1-2 hours in blazing sun, no shade whatsoever, very inhuman

- If you have multiple persons, ticket office wants to see them all before selling tickets to you, to avoid frauds

- When you finally get your ticket, you have to wait another 1-2 hours, before you are allowed to enter

- If possible, use private tickets, not guided tour. Guided tour waiting time in security check is unbelievably long

- take plenty of water with you, another set of indian "gentlemens" will try to rip you off with water bottles (3-5 eur each). There is only one water faucet to refill your bottle...

- be aware, that you are not allowed in shade of the 2-3 trees surrounding Colosseum, security and police will force you to leave the shade and whoopdidoo back to the blazing hot sun

Now, for the Colosseum itself. It still is a magnificent marvel of engineering and build quality. The idea of cool air under the pillars still works and it feels great.
The site itself is a bit overengineered, too many display stands, bookstores blocking the view of actual walls of this great structure.

All and all a little too small bang for the buck and unimaginable waiting time. In my opinion, you will get a better experience walking around it...

title: Avoid Show Me Italy Tours
text:
Rome: Colosseum Underground, Arena Floor and Ancient Rome: Several days prior to our tour, we were notified that the underground portion of the tour had ben cancelled. We were flying out to Rome the next day and really didn't have the time to dig too deeply into the matter. After several annoying, 'what do you wanna do' emails, we chose to take the alternative tour offered rather than the full refund as we had our entire Rome tour schedule booked with a driver and guides. We were offered the...Rome: Colosseum Underground, Arena Floor and Ancient Rome tour MINUS the underground portion of the tour. The tour began 5 minutes after the originally scheduled tour. The original tour cost Euro 629.40 (@$705USD for 6 people)
     Our tour began with the Ancient Rome portion. This consisted of a 2+ hour walking lecture of the ancient Roman Forum area in 93 degreeF blistering heat and unreal crowds. NOT FUN. We then walked entirely around the outside of the Colosseum only to enter a seriously long queue (30+ minutes) for our "SKIP THE LINE COLOSSEUM TICKETS! Once inside the colosseum, we made our way to the arena floor and were allowed approximately 20 minutes to take pictures. It was at this point that we said 'enough' and left the tour. As we left there were only about 5 people left of the original 20-25 person group. It took us almost another 30 minutes to find the only available exit from the colosseum. 
     I was given a partial refund of @30% of the tour cost for our trouble. After the tour was complete, I noticed that our electronic tickets had been changed to reflect a different tour than what we had originally booked with the ticket price now
showing the original price minus refund. Never we we told this was to be some sort of educational lecture or that the ancient Rome portion of the tour would be conducted first. As with many people, we had planned to limit our time in the Forum area due to its dry subject matter and time constraints.
     I had heard that many of these tour operators offer tours with tickets to venues that they DO NOT HAVE but plan to get later when the tickets are offered to the general public. They have a distinct advantage during ticket sales due to computerized buying programs and the fact that tickets for these tours are offered exactly 30 days prior to the tour....down to the minute. For example, if you want a ticket to the 10:00 am Underground Colosseum tour on 31 July 2023, those tickets would be put on sale on 1 July 2023 at 10:00 am......ROME TIME!!! This means the tickets are available to me in the Midwest US at 03:00 am 30 June 2023 at which time I can attempt to get 6 tix, competing with numerous computer programs to do so. Not very consumer friendly if you ask me.
     All in all, I think my refund was much too low considering, and they never told us what the new tour would actually be as I would assume most people would say no to the offer. Last minute changes like this to a larger group's touring schedule tends to elicit the desired acceptance to new tour offers. I was duped. Too late for me, but not for you. DO NOT USE "Show Me Italy Tours" who is one of the vendors supplying "Get Your Guide Italy." Be forewarned, I'd give it zero stars if I could still write a review!

title: Gidsrome oplichting
text: Rondleiding geboekt bij GidsRome. Werd een dag van te voren afgemeld ivm ziekte van de tourgids. Zouden geld terugkrijgen maar u raad het al. Nooit mogen ontvangen. Heer is ook niet meer te bereiken en reageert nergens op. Meer mensen hebben helaas de zelfde ervaring. Dus niet meer boeken als ik u was.

title: Collosseum 2023
text: Visit historical site was good .we had booked a excursion which was very vague .The 2nd part of trip takes you into Roman Forum were the host dud not show up si we was left to explore  the ruins on out iwn

title: Messy place
text:
The local government really has to clean this place up - too many scammy tour guides and people with bracelets that run up to you to try to make money. And they get mad at you if you try to mess with them!

Could have been a fun place to visit but unfortunately it was ruined by the people there.

title: Bellissimo ma personale pietoso
text: Il Colosseo è molto bello e l’esperienza con il tour operator è stata perfetta. Il voto è basso per la qualità del personale all’ingresso ed addetto alla sicurezza: maleducazione, arroganza, inglese appena passabile. Non dovrebbero lavorare a contatto con dei turisti. La differenza tra svolgere il proprio mestiere con il sorriso sulle labbra e svolgere lo stesso mestiere con l’attitudine che ho subito io è solo ed esclusivamente l’effetto. Il turista non torna, perché pensa che tutti gli italiani siano maleducati e di quel livello….una cosa indegna

title: sämsta köer
text: just nu verkar alla besöka colosseum och tunnelbanan är proppfull och långa köer hos objekten, helst tidigt där

title: WATCH OUT FOR PICK POCKETER'S
text: Be very, very ..... careful for your valuables ( cash, credit cards) pick pocketer's are so professional there... with a blink of an eye they steel and can ruin your whole vacation .... this is a spoken so much , yet it can't be stopped !!

title: Negativa
text: Caos Caos Caos e grazie all'organizzazione cittadina ancora caos. File interminabili e per chi come me ha deciso di visitare Roma all'ultimo momento prenotazioni per entrare online a partire da metà luglio. Visto solo esternamente

title: Incroyable d'un point de vue extérieur
text:
Beaucoup moins une fois à l'intérieur où c'est blindé de touristes, de guides et d'expositions de tout un tas de morceaux de ci ou de ça.

On retrouve à mon goût beaucoup trop de matériaux d'aujourd'hui qui viennent dénaturer le lieu (tableaux, bancs, barrières, ascenseurs)....

Difficile pour moi de me projeter dans "l'ancien temps" et imaginer la vie telle qu'elle fut pour les gladiateurs

Une assez grosse déception

title: Toilets were filthy and the attendant man was very aggressive and rude, the colosseum itself was nice to see
text: It was nice seeing the colosseum however my little one needed the toilet so off we went, it was €1 to use the facilities (i would assume this was for the upkeep of the toilets) the attendant man on the turn gates we’re extremely rude and aggressive shouting at young girls if they was struggling with putting the coins in and wouldn’t help, I was charged twice even though I just had to go in with my little one. On entry the place were absolutely disgusting it had never been cleaned, there was brown stuff dripping all into the toilet roll people didn’t know if it was poo or rust from the toilet holders. The floor was wet through, door didn’t have lock just piece of string. The man was then shouting at everyone to get out, get out when we’re washing hands to let more people in. Needs a visit of the health n hygiene people and the man needs sacking

title: I may give the Colosseum a second chance...
text:
We toured the Colosseum only because we wanted the ticket to get into the Forum for a private tour.  To be honest, the idea of the Colosseum as a death venue grossed me out.  We purchased the English audio tour.  The crowds were unbearable so we didn't even try to follow the route of the tour!  Instead, we found a quiet (sort of) place to sit, and played through the entire tour.  It was well done and took about 45 minutes.  Had no interest in going up or down a level and fighting the crowds, group tours, etc.  We just stayed near the entrance the entire time.  

Our guide for the Forum chewed me out and said the Colosseum is an amazing place if only for the architecture.  Next time I'll do the private tour of the Colosseum with Mirabilia Urbis tours.

title: Extremely over crowded
text: Very over crowded.  Skip the line tickets will still see you queuing for over an hour.  Overly officious Colosseum staff.  Avoid in busy season.  Walk around the outside, take a few photos, then get out of there!

title: Tout sauf Tripadvisor
text: Tripadvisor n’a pas été arrangeant du tout alors que nous avons pas réussi à nous rendre sur place à l’heure pour la visite du fait que le tour d’Italie arrivait à Rome ce jour là. Aucun remboursement n’a été fait suite à notre demande. Pour faire de la pub ils sont bons, pour le reste il y a personne donc je vous conseille de passer par un autre site pour vos réservations

title: TRE ORE DI CODA SOTTO IL SOLE, COLOSSEO IN MANO AI TOUR OPERATOR
text: Un mese che cerco di acquistare 4 biglietti per il Colosseo e non ci si riesce. Poi una volta arrivati li ho capito come funziona. Il Colosseo è in mano ai tour operators che si comprano migliaia di biglietti e se li rivendono al triplo del prezzo nei loro siti, peggio ancora se vuoi entrare un tour guidato per 4 persone con guida costa 200 euro altrimenti ti fai una bella coda SOTTO AL SOLE DI TRE ORE dove saresti disposto a tutto a comprare un ombrellino a 10 euro per salvarti da un'insolazione o una bottiglia di acqua a 2 euro. Il Comune deve mettere uno STOP A QUESTO ANDAZZO e permettere di comprare i biglietti on line , un tetto all'acquisto dei biglietti da parte di questi grandi tour.

title: zeer mooi en indrukwekkend MAAR SUPER DRUK
text: was er super druk binnen willen zou ons eenwachtrij van 3 tot 4 uur duren of anders voor veel extra geld met een speciale gids maar aangezien je naar binnen kan kijken zagen we dat het gewoon file lopen is met duizenden andere

title: Awful staff! Disgusted
text: Staff were awful! Tubes were down so we were 10 minutes late for our allotted slot and they wouldn’t let us in. They laughed in our faces and were smoking and blowing it at us. Absolutely disgusting. Contacted them directly to speak to them about it and never received a reply.

title: This company is horrible
text: This is a horribly run business and I recommend you look elsewhere. I booked two tours and they screwed up both. They are incompetent and shady. They said they had a technical issue with one tour and we found out it was overbooked and we were bumped last minute. Run from them.

title: Disorganised chaos.
text: Absolutely chaotic. Poor organisation and signage. Too many people allowed in at once and groups just cause even more delays. The bottom tier is extra but they don't make that clear at all when you buy a ticket. Staff unhelpful when you are not sure which was to go. I actually wouldn't recommend the stress.

title: Disappointed in Italy
text: We set up our skip the line tickets to the colosseum a few months ahead of the trip. On the day of the reservation (3 hours before the reservation) I get a message that we were cancelled. There is nothing we can do now. The place is booked through our trip.

title: Disappointed in new policy
text: We had this tour booked 11 months in advance for our group of 13 people with Perillo tours for today. We had the skip the line pass too. Last night at 7 pm we got a call from our travel agent that there’s a new policy in place where they no longer accept the skip the line or honor this as of June 1. So for everyone who has this already booked beware. We were unable to go into the colosseum now as we couldn’t wait the 2-3 hours online due to our whole day being booked with other tours. We were able to walk around the outside but honestly we were very disappointed. We really wanted to see the inside and were upset with the way this was handled. As for the colosseum it’s an incredible landmark, even just from the outside. The area around is very crowded and very dirty. It’s a shame this beautiful piece of history has so much trash surrounding it.

title: Building magnificent ( from outside
text:
We visited on 2nd June - Republic Day.
Queued for hours to enter at 2pm only to be told ....even though advertised as FREE on a public holiday we still needed to queue at office for a FREE TICKET ! inorder to enter.
Staff unhelpful.
Signage poor.

title: Obras en todo su entorno
text:
Lastima pero esta de obras alrededor y en frente hace muchos anos, asi que hay que disfrutarla a pesar de las vayas de obras, sacos de construccion etc
Es un icono precioso de la ciudad de Roma que hay que visitar este como este

title: Ruim
text: Infelizmente adquirir um bilhete direto no site do Coliseu é quase impossível. Estou começando a acreditar que dependemos de cambista/agências para isso. Mal abre a data e todos os ingressos já aparecem com indisponiveis, sem contar que ao longo do dia vai abrindo algumas vagas e em segundos some e mesmo quando vc está com os bilhetes no carrinho e vai formalizar o pagamento já aparece que foram vendidos. Parece que é tudo armado para que vc não adquira os bilhetes diretamente no site do Coliseu.

title: Queues and queues and queues followed by congestion inside.
text: What a great place ruined by queues and hoards. Keep clear of this place. Just awful queues to get in (even when you have bought a skip the queues tour) and when you get in you are beset by hoards. Such a massive disappointment.

title: Know before you go
text:
The staff and security teams don’t seem to have ever dealt with tourists before. They’re belligerence and lack of basic crowd management skills was stunning. Zero stars for that.

We also got stuck a Viator (violator is a better name) ticket scalping scam that didn’t help the situation. Zero stars for that.

The Coliseum itself is a marvel. It’s more than I ever expected and I had to keep reminding myself I was really there. Our evening tour guide was great. That gets 5 stars.

My advice? Book directly through the Coliseum, go in knowing the security and visitor staff is disorganized/not ready to deal with the public, and but that all behind you once you get inside as it is truly a marvel and worth it. 

Just go direct. No Violator or other scalpers.

title: Inaccettabile
text: Il prezzo pagato è assolutamente inaccettabile per quello che poi si vede all l'interno. Assolutamente non consigliato nei weekend. Non raccomandiamo di comprare i biglietti in anticipo, costano troppo come abbiamo detto.

title: Stress at the Colosseum
text: The history of the Colosseum blows me away, but the crowds, even at 10.00am, were hard to bear and the tour tours are very frustrating. We chose to look around ourselves, but it wasn’t signed well, so we selected audio tours.  The voice was pompous and boring, so that wasn’t great.  Other people jostle you, even when you’re trying to take photos, which was frankly annoying

title: Απογοητευση
text: Απογοήτευση. Περίμενα καιρό αυτό το ταξίδι.  Μένω 30 χρόνια Βερολίνο. Έχω ταξιδέψει σε πολλά μέρη. Πότε δεν χάρηκα τόσο την ημέρα της επιστροφής. 4στερο ξενοδοχείο που ούτε καν για 1 δεν άξιζε. Ανεδαιστατοι σερβιτόροι σε όλη τη Ρώμη. Σκουπίδια σε κάθε γωνιά της πόλης. Οι Ιταλοί αποφεύγουν κάθε ερώτηση τουρίστα.  Πανάκριβα εισιτήρια σε αρχαιολογικά μνημεία. Και για αποχαιρετηστηριο, νας ζητησαν στο αεροδρομια να πληρωσουμε πληρωμενη βαλιτσα.Ελλάδα και πάλι Ελλάδα.

title: Overrated Tourist Destination
text: Overrated. Too crowded. You can’t even take a decent photo because it’s like being inside a sardines can, could barely move and the lines were too long. I regretted coming here. The photos you see online are 1000x different in reality.

title: Poor Ticketing Options
text: Very interesting and a must see if you are in Rome. The only downsides are how difficult it is to buy tickets (no tickets available at the attraction) and there is a lot of modern brickwork.

title: Tra cantieri e Orda turistica
text: Una delle fermate della metro più suggestive al mondo. Nel viso di tutti proprio tutti appena usciti dall'underground si scorge la meraviglia negli occhi di chi guarda questa maestosità. Ma i lavori per la metro  non aiutano alla gestione del flusso immenso di turisti.

title: Cheapest tickets purchaised
text:
Due to cheapest tickets no access to arena floor or under the coliseum 
Big disappointment. 
Defo pay more for the full experience 

Also worth paying for a guided tour as so much not said on the recorded tour 
Not the collisions fault. We didn’t discuss what we wanted from the experience and did get what we payed for

title: Rushed Palatine Hill was a stupid idea.  Don't do combined tour.
text:
We did "Skip the Line: Colosseum, Roman Forum & Palatine Hill Guided Tour".

Palatine Hill was first.  It was extremely rushed.
  We even lost a family who couldn't keep up..

Guide showed the first 5 people things from his book, and the other 20 saw nothing.
I have no idea what we were looking at, because guide had no time to answer questions and we were too far away to know which building he was pointing at.
Guide kept saying "take pictures and I'll tell you later" but sometimes he did not.
Someone asked a question and he said "I'll tell you later", but he did not.
This was because the coliseum tickets were timed too soon, and we had to run to the coliseum line.
  Forum and Palatine Hill were ruined for us.
Don't do this tour with 25 people. 
 It left 5 minutes early, and there was not adequate time for the Forum and Palatine hill.
Organization running tour put stress on everyone, by ordering Colosseum tickets timed too early..

title: Huge crowds wrecked the experience!
text:
In itself the Colosseum was all that it should have been. Exceptional historical site. 
However the huge crowds and queues largely spoiled the magic. Even with tickets and hardly any queuing once inside the numbers inside were insane. What a turn off. 
Probably no different to any other site of historical interest in this overpopulated over commercialised world. Trevi fountain; Spanish Steps; Vatican same thing

title: Horrible
text: We booked a tour for coliseum in Rome. The tour guide didn’t show up I called the company twice. They told us to go to the entrance if coliseum. We did The man at gate said we didn’t have tickets. I showed him our voucher. He still wouldn’t let us in. Fortunately another tour guide came to us and asked if our guide didn’t show. She said that happens a lot. She included us in her tour(for extra cost). Trip advisor was contacted by our credit card company and Trip advisor said we didn’t show!  We were there. They didn’t show up!  Trip advisor will not refund the money. Our first tour guide was wonderful. My advice is to book with a company from the place you are going

title: Beware: Local restaurants scam customers and gangs of pickpockets in metro station
text:
BE VERY CAREFUL - THEY HAVE VERY REAL PETTY CRIME PROBLEMS IN AND AROUND COLLOSEUM

Take care of restaurant scam....

My partner and I visited a local restaurant just in front of Colloseum. We ordered 2 glasses of red wine. The waiter was over friendly in pushing us into accepting a bottle of red wine. We said firmly "no, only two glasses". Next, an over friendly waitress approached our table and opened a bottle of red wine saying "you ordered wine". Once opened and sitting at table, surrounded by people, and tired from lots of walking through Rome we just said yes and accepted bottle. When bill arrived it was €100 for the bottle. In that situation we were effectively trapped since we had "accepted" the bottle. When I questioned bill I was told waitress had offered us the most expensive bottle in their restaurant. Also, they know full well if complain on social media then they can afford not to care since every hour there are literally tens of thousands of hapless tourists unknowingly walking past restaurants who will unwittingly stop (and be vulnerable to same scam)

It is a well know scam: the restaurant effectively corners you and because unthinkingly you have accepted the open bottle then if reported to police or complaint then it will not be upheld - it is a subtle rip off.

To make matters worse as we caught metro train at Colloseum metro station my partner had her wallet and credit cards stolen by pickpockets as we boarded train.

title: Colosseum group tour
text: booked with arena tours..Lots of waiting around whilst groups were moved from one place to the next.  The skip the queue to get in was ok. Guide was very good and informative.

title: Crowded, Crowded.
text:
I would like to say this was an enjoyable visit, but I cannot.
Tour guide did their best but it was too crowded to enjoy.

title: Ne réservez pas avec Headout!
text: Trop déçue, j'ai  réservé trois billets il y a des mois pour ma visite dans 5 jours au Colisée via Headout. Ils n'ont pas honoré la réservation et après avoir tenté de les joindre à plusieurs reprises sans succès et de demander d'émettre le billet ils n'ont rien trouvé de mieux que de me dire qu'ils étaient désolés qu'ils avaient vendus nos places et ne pouvaient plus nous en proposer, pour me dédomager ils m'ont offert 4€ à valoir sur une autre réservation! Foutage de geule total! Résultat: plus rien de disponible si près du jour de la visite. Trop dégoûtée!!!

title: Monument incontournable mais manque de confort.
text:
Monument incontournable de Rome, à visiter absolument.
On regrette cependant le manque de bancs à l’extérieur pour se reposer et aussi un manque criant de toilettes, surtout pour les femmes.
L’audio guide n’a pas assez insisté sur la construction et le bâtiment lui-même, selon nous.

title: Roma pass seule inutile pour réserver le Colisée
text:
Carta pass achetée avant le départ et impossibilité de réserver… 
Ayant vécu à Rome et y étant revenue plusieurs fois, La dolce vità s’est muée en piège à touristes, comme la côte d’Azur. Perte d’âme et de relations humaines. C’est vraiment dommage..

title: When in Rome you have to go.
text:
It has to be done, but bear in mind, even with a guided tour, its likley you have to queue at places. Not anywhere near as dense as the Vatican Museum, but still very busy. 

Great to hear about how its use has changed over the years, as well as demonstrating mans inhumanity to man, nothing changes!

title: Scam, fraud
text: This tour guide is a total scam and fraud. We were two people who booked the tour for Colosseum. We went to the meeting point on exact time, but they were not present and they never arrived. After that we searched whole area around the Colosseum but we never found the tour guide. I suggest you all to stay away and do not book with this company. Otherwise they will take your money and will disappear.

title: Underestimated
text:
I will be totally honest, like always.
The Coloseum is overrated and too touristy.
I don't think visiting the Colosseum is worthing 16.00€. The price is too high and there are many other things you can to during your visit in Rome. And for free.
For example Piazza Di Spagnia, Fontana Di Trevi,The Vatican (St. Peter's Basilicais free too) and many other things.
But you should 100% visit it at least from outside. The best time is at noght so you can see it illumonated.

title: Not what you think
text:
I wouldn't bother buying tickets. We had tickets but went on the wrong day, so we walked round and was really disappointed. It's not as it looks online, it's very built up around it and a lot of it has been remade  
My friend booked a tour for herself and her husband. Her tour guide was late and only stayed with the group for 10 minutes.

title: Entorno del Coliseo no adaptado a carritos de bebé, ni sillas de ruedas ni la masificación de peatones.
text:
El Coliseo es impresionante. Un lujo que se haya conservado hasta nuestros días.

No obstante, nuestra experiencia en los entornos del Coliseo en particular y Roma en general, no fue buena al menos desde la perpectiva del que va con un carrito de bebé (y peor sería si vas en silla de ruedas). Las esquinas de las aceras no están rebajadas de forma adecuada para carritos y mucho menos para personas con sillas de ruedas.  Era necesario ir con el carrito (igual que el resto de gente) andando por la carretera (sobre todo entorno al Coliseo). Nada peligroso, en comparación con cruzar un paso se zebra. Ahí si que te la juegas. Da igual llevar un carrito con un bebé. Nunca vi algo turístico tan masificado. Faltan calles peatonales en Roma. Mínimo, entorno del Coliseo.

title: More Insane Crowds
text: This monument is extraordinary but the real experience is that of the throngs of people, the giant crowds, the fences, gates, guards, and the rules.

title: Personale incompetente
text: Fare corso di formazione al personale per approccio positivo al cliente. La signora alla cassa non conosceva neanche i tipi abbonamento. Abbiamo dovuto spiegarlo noi

title: Valt wel mee
text: Had er meer van verwacht. Mensen die je lastig vallen voor een kaartje en eenmaal binnen viel het wel mee. Er zijn andere plekken wat naar mijn mening indrukwekkender waren in Rome.

title: Beeindruckend, aber nur überlaufen
text: Man muss bei dem Gebäude bedenken, wann es gebaut wurde. Daher ist es schon beeindruckend. Aber beeindruckend sind viele Gebäude(komplexe) in Rom. Sicherlich ist es mit das beste Foto(Selfie) Motiv (von außen). Innen ist es einfach nur überfüllt. Tipp: Die besten Fotos kann man, meiner Meinung, vom Forum Romanum machen.

title: Réserver obligatoirement en ligne à l'avance
text:
Impossible d'acheter un billet pour le Colisée sur place, en avril 2023, malgré ce qui est indiqué sur certains sites ou forums. Nous sommes arrivés en famille (2 adultes et 2 enfants), tôt avant l'ouverture, et on nous a indiqué (demande faite auprès du bureau des ventes) qu'il n'y avait plus aucune place en vente depuis plusieurs semaines. Il faut impérativement réserver un billet en ligne très en avance (nous avons tenté 15 jours avant et c'était déjà trop tard...), ou faire le choix d'une visite avec un guide (40€/adulte et 20€/enfant), qu'on peut réserver sur place, et qui inclus le billet d'entrée. 
Nous avons donc pris uniquement le billet pour le forum et le palatin, sur place, à 18€/adulte.

title: site pas sérieux
text:
ayant réservé une visite, celle ci a été annulée la veille (guide malade) et on ne m'a proposé aucune autre : soi disant pas de place. Bref je suis rentrée de Rome sans l'avoir vu
SITE ABSOLUMENT PAS SERIEUX

title: 沉浸历史
text: 觉得还可以吧 可以感受下历史的遗迹，沉浸其中。最好在夜晚点起火把 一个人参观，感受会更深刻。体会下几千年前古人的感受。

title: Pesimq
text:
Ojo!! connlas entradas.
Headout, nos estafó.  Noa vendieron entradas a centenares de personas  y no se pudo entrar una vergüenza. 
Esto  sucedió  entre 7 y 8 de abril de 2023.
Seguramente  sucedió  muchas más!
No comprar nada a Headout.
Vergüenza, no solo robo  de plata sino de la ilusión  y posibilidad de conocer este tipo de Lugar.
Quizá  muchos nunca mas lo piedan realizar 
No comprar a Headout

title: Rude and inexperienced staff at Colosseum
text: On crutches after a recent knee operation but did not wish family to miss out on the full Rome experience. Purchased relatively expensive Skip The Line tickets 4 days in advance of visit. Got separated on tour when staff refused my family access to lift (despite having 1 other person only in large lift). Unfortunately stairs do not come near where lift is. Left in labyrinth trying to find my way to exit to find my family. Kids were very stressed as I took a very long time to reach them given my mobility issues (crutches). Staff were super unhelpful. Would not permit me to take a short cut to the exit despite my explanation. Apparently I had not paid the extra fee to access this part of the Colisseum.  Could not care less about the tour at this stage as was in real pain and needed to exit. Added 40 mins to time needed to reach the exit point. Spoke to 4 staff members in total. All but 1 were super rude.  Unskilled in customer service and bereft of any compassion for disabled person. AVOID THIS VENUE AT ALL COSTS if you have small children or have any mobility constraints. Second time visiting and definitely my last

title: Its a Scam be aware
text: Its a scam. Don't waste your Money booking this very experience guided tour. All other tours start outside the Colosseum Metro. Not Tiqets, they meet up over 2km from the venue. Our taxi was stuck in traffic. Tried to cancel as couldn't reach start point on time. We ended up paying again, but much cheaper rate for much better tour from outside the venue. Tigets will not refund. Scaming tourists everyday. Be aware. Its so much cheaper to arrange outside with a tour that actually exists.

title: ROMA PASS ??? No,no,nooooo !!!
text: Dopo aver comprato il Roma Pass, vengo a conoscenza che per visitare il Colosseo bisogna prenotare e fino a qui non ci sono problemi; il problema è che le prenotazioni vanno oltre i 25 GG.In breve la società che gestisce Roma Pass ha liberamente frodato gli utenti. Burini, che ti aspetti !!!

title: A huge disappointment
text:
I'm quite a huge fan of ancient history, museums and exhibitions. I was looking forward to get onto the Palantkne Hill, Forum Romanum or the colosseum. Neither one was accessible due to a pointless booking system where sometimes times lots are available and then some 10 seconds later aren't anymore. No one at the the gates where helpful or trying to assist.
The next ticket available is in 14 days? Do one really has to book that much in advance. Pardon my french, but get your **** together. Rome, you can do so much better.

title: Do not visit it on holidays - it may be a closed area. Be careful not to visit this site on holidays.
text:
We took a lot of photos. It was a magical place. You can take a lot of photos but be careful when there are a lot of people. 
Be careful not to visit this site on holidays. It may be closed around this area and the transportation might be canceled.

title: Colosseum in ruins
text:
Open all the ticket booths they were not been used and the tours were all booked and overpriced. The tour we had was very expensive and the head sets did not work . The prices on the giant billboards surrounding the colosseum were advertising the wrong prices. Plus the wait time was 2 hours .we left the tour and did our own thing.
 The actual colosseum is fantastic but getting in a nightmare. I suggest you go 1hour before closing. Everything was confusing and chaotic.

title: Fantastic but avoid the "Tourist Sharks" selling "skip the line" tickets
text:
The Colosseum is an impressive structure and well presented as a museum.  Fascinating to see it for real and appreciate the magnitude of the whole building.  This is a must see when in Rome.   

The visit was spoiled however by the 'tourist sharks' prowling around outside offering 'skip the queue' tickets.  We were totally taken in by them as they wear very authentic looking "official guide" lanyards, and flash a screen of the official booking website up showing no available slots for that day.  After we'd paid more than DOUBLE for their 'guided tour', I went online and found out there were still plenty of tickets available within the next hour or two and for less than half the price we'd just paid.    Bottom line is - don't get drawn in by their spiel, go to the official website and book your tickets well in advance (even the day before is possible).  If you're travelling during peak times I'd suggest booking your tickets before you leave for Italy.   

We continued on the tour anyway.  The tour guide was using a childs book of pictures and pointing out the key features on the outside of the Colosseum, and went on for about half an hour.  we realised he was having to use up time until the entrance time on the tickets.  When we did finally get to the gate there was a problem as there were too many in our group and they had to ask some people to go a different entrance. 

Once inside we chose to go our own way rather than follow the tour guide who was really not giving any more information than was already available on the museum boards and information points.  We wanted to go at our own pace.  

Well worth visiting, just go the office website route to pay for your entrance.

title: Monumentales Bauwerk, ohne Führung fast sinnlos
text: Der Besuch gehört irgendwie dazu, aber es gibt schönere Attraktionen in Rom. Ist man erst einmal mit dem Ticket drin, vorbei an den dubiosen Ticketverkäufern, wird man relativ schnell ernüchtert. Eigentlich wird man mit den Massen durchgeschoben, kaum Erklärungen vorhanden wenn man kein Audio Guide kauft.

title: dehors suffit
text: endroit agréable beaucoup de monde, la visite a intérieur n'apporte pas grand chose privilégié le forum romain et le mont paladine.

title: Ageist
text: Wouldn't let my kids in because they looked over 18 when we even gave them evidence and they STILL refused. Just because their father is tall and they have the genes. Holiday. Ruined.

title: Kind of Disappoiting
text: Difficult to access. Long queues. The landmark itself was disappointing. Smaller than expected. Would have not gone had I knew what it really was.

title: Ciudad masificada una pena
text:
