When inside the experience was dampened by pushy tours guides, once again they are pushy and rude. 

I’ve visited many amazing spectacles and this is one. However Italy really need to get a grip of it before everyone’s experience is ruined.

title: Too touristic, loads of SPAM
text:
With so many crappy salesmen and saleswoman, I was just waiting for 5 Nigerian princes to come over to tell me I would receive loads of money from them. 

The city should really do something about the overload of street vendors. You’ll get harassed every 2 steps. It’s ridiculous and annoying. 

The coliseum is an impressive building though.

title: Be prepared to be bombarded by ticket sellers
text:
The outside of the Colosseum is definitely a must see when Rome, however the amount of people trying to sell you tickets is beyond ridiculous. We tried ignoring them or pretending that we didn’t speak English but we sell ended up being ripped off and on a tour. We initially ignored the guy but he said he worked for the Colosseum. We had no idea who to believe by this stage so we just bought the tickets and went on a tour. 

The inside of the Colosseum was very crowded even though it’s the off season. As soon as our tour ended and we took some pictures we were out of there.

title: Trop d'attente sous un soleil de plomb !!!
text: Il nous fallait du courage et une bonne motivation pour affronter la file d'attente interminable sous un soleil de plomb !!! Les curieux et passionnés seront récompensés par ces vestiges... dans le cas contraire, il vaudrait mieux s'orienter vers une autre dépense de temps et de budget. A chacun son voyage...

title: Indrukwekkend
text: Te verwachten: druk, maar het viel mee. Goed georganiseerd bij de ingang, indrukwekkend om te zien..

title: You are left to imagine
text: Certainly a ruin... you are left to imagine everything at the flava... impressive construction by the Romans... but hope to see Italy restoring the amphitheater

title: Des travaux...
text:
Mouais...c'est sûr le monument est imposant et assez joli. Mais la déception est présente quand on y entre: des travaux, des échafaudages... le Colisée ferme 1h avant le coucher du soleil donc il faut bien se renseigner avant d'y aller. Les billets coupe-file sont indispensables pour une entrée certaine. Beaucoup de rabatteurs pour un billet à 15€/tête, si vous êtes pressés de rentrer (comme nous), prenez le les yeux fermés. Le guide nous a fait rentrer en groupe et une fois dedans, libre à vous de suivre ou pas le groupe...
Sympa mais faire 3h de queue pour ça...je ne pense pas. Il y a bien mieux et plus intéressant dans la ville.

title: Boring
text: One thin you will find about the roman empire.... the remains which were once incredible are now just ruble!  The colosum is a stop on the road but I would not make this a focal point much better things to see in Rome

title: A must see, but beware of misleading online tickets!
text:
The Colosseum itself is a must see, and probably my favourite site in Rome. We went first thing in the morning and it wasn't too crowded and fun to walk around. I imagine going early or late in the day would be most beneficial to avoid crowds, and get good lighting if taking pictures (and in the Summer to avoid the heat). Absolutely can't go to Rome and not see the Colosseum!

HOWEVER, be very careful about which tickets you buy on the Colosseum website. They offer a ridiculous amount of options, but many contain little to no description of what is included. We booked the Entry ticket + Panorama which we thought would give us access to the upper level for better pictures. When we arrived we were advised you can only go up there with a tour group, and that we needed to be at the site at a specific time to go up with the guide. This was NOT listed on the description of the ticket when purchased, and nothing on the ticket itself mentions a guided tour, just the time to be at the Colosseum. When asking security about it, they advised us of the need to go up with a guide, but that they get this question often (probably because their site is horrible...), and when we went to the ticket desk to see if we could at least go on another tour or get a partial refund, they just said the meeting time was on the ticket, and a misunderstanding that we had to accept, even though nothing outlines a guided tour or need for one.

Buying a ticket in advance IS beneficial as you only have to go through the security line, and not the ticket line first. But I can't honestly advise on how to book the features you want and gain information on these prior to arriving, as their website is simply horrible and lacks any real description of what is provided or requirements upon arrival. In the end it was €8 down the drain for us which isn't the end of the world, but more importantly we missed out on a feature and view we were really looking forward to. For many people this is a once in a lifetime visit, and to not properly outline the inclusions and requirement of more expensive tickets is simply lazy and shows a lack of care for their visitors.

To the staff at the Colosseum, if you would like someone to update your ticket descriptions, please let me know, and I'll be happy to help! A few extra sentences would only take a few minutes to type up, and would go a long way to provide future visitors pleasant experiences at what is truly one of the most impressive sights in the world!

title: Огромные очереди
text:
Огромные очереди, и честно говоря, ничего особенного. В Риме есть гораздо более грандиозные сооружения. В любом случае, увидеть такое культовое место захочет каждый. 
Не ведитесь на уличных продавцов билетов!!! Билеты нужно покупать только в специализированных кассах.

title: Fint
text: En del kø, mange selgere utenfor. Du trenger også egen billett for å dra i andre etasjer, som var litt kjipt.. ellers veldig fint å ha vært der!

title: Overbearing, stressful, disorganised
text: The Colosseum itself is beautiful, rich in history and magnificent to see, but the area absolutely ruins the experience for me. My partner and I had booked tickets online (coop culture) and upon arrival we were bombarded with people asking us to buy tickets from them. We said every time we had tickets and tried to move on. Nobody would tell us the correct place to go to collect our tickets. After joining several wrong queues we finally found the right one. The girl told us we needed to run to make it on time, but we had to wait in a security line for 15 minutes, and then we couldn’t find any signs for the guide meeting point. We ended up being too late for our guided tour, despite having arrived about 50 minutes before it was due to start. Perhaps if we had booked with another company they may have guided us properly, but the area is so disorganised and stressful that it really takes from the experience.

title: Over priced
text: It is still a wonderful piece of architecture but I felt a bit ripped off. The 12 euros basic entry gives you a walk around a few levels. There are long lines and even if you have tickets the security is slow. There should be more information boards around and especially as you are in line. We enjoyed it but I would spend the money on your own guide and do this in a more costly manner next time.

title: emblème de la ville
text: c’est l’emblème de la ville mais la visite est un peu décevante si vous prenez l’audio guide : 5,50 euros pour 6 commentaires qui sont trop longs et pas très intéressants, quel dommage de ne pas rendre ça plus dynamique !

title: Coliseu
text: Apesar das manutenções e restaurações, imaginei que estaria em melhores condições de preservação. Fiquei um pouco frustrado.

title: Passage obligé
text: Lors de notre visite de la ville à pied, nous sommes arrivés devant le colisée. Nous sommes malheureusement restés à l'extérieur vu les files d'attente. Actuellement en plein chantier à plusieurs endroits, la ville de Rome est infestée de chantier ainsi que de machines et appareils quelconque. De plus, il y a énormément de touristes. Impossible de visiter correctement les différents sites. Nous avons vu le colisée de l'extérieur.

title: האיטלקים יודעים לעשות כסף מתיירים
text: היינו בקולוסיאום. ללא ספק מסלול חובה למי שמגיע לרומא. המקום גדול ומפואר, לידו חובה לבקר בפורום ובשער טיטוס עם כל . ההיסטוריה של העם שלנו. יחד עם זאת, לנו יש בארץ מקומות יותר עתיקים ויותר יפים (הכותל למשל) שהם בחינם ואילו הקולוסיאום עולה 22 יורו. לתשומתלבכם

title: Bello da lontano..
text: In prossimità del Colosseo ci sono i lavori della metropolitana brutti da vedere e fastidiosi al suono. Intorno è circondato da transenne e ci sono solo turisti, bagarini e venditori abusivi. Non si capisce nulla.

title: Decepção
text: Havia uma expectativa bem melhor, porém, lotado, muito abandono, muita coisa preparada para turistas, muito fora da realidade.  Sem falar que venderam os tickets sem avisar que eles valem para o foro romano também. Aí a maioria vai em busca do segundo ingresso.

title: Pretty amazing
text: It's worth it to have a guide, but book one ahead of time. You will be accosted by tour guides outside the colosseum. They have shirts that make it look like "staff" but they are not!

title: The street sellers ruined the experience
text:
We were so looking forward to this more than anything. 
As we approached the colosseum on a beautiful sunny day, we were met by a swarm of street touts trying to sell us tickets. It was absolutely ludicrous. It was awful. In all the cities, I have never experienced such an onslaught of harassment. 
Because of this one particular issue, which is at most attractions, it’s completely put us off Rome again. 
The Colosseum itself had no sign posts outside, didn’t tell you where to queue or where to go. 
Totally badly organised. 
Once in, your left alone, but beware it’s busy. 
You can’t visit everywhere, there’s extra fees! Surprising . 
It is an amazing archeological site but your still restricted what you can do.

title: Nothing special
text: Was looking forward to seeing this piece of history but sadly it was a big let down!! First, there were so many of those ‘staff’ workers trying to sell you skip the line tickets just to make extra money. You may have skipped the line to get to security quicker but you lined up with everyone else to get tickets! Second, it’s a shame to see the Colosseum in such a dirty and neglected state. Rubbish everywhere and gum spat all over the ground. It’s obvious that the people of Rome do not care much about this piece of history compared to their churches which are spectacular. And lastly, as you exit prepare to be bombarded by African Americans trying to sell you junk.

title: Okay, Staff benimmt sich allerdings sehr genervt...
text: Grundsätzlich schön es live zu sehen, ist halt aber Massentourismus par excellence..so verhalten sich auch die Wärter 30min vor Schließung....

title: I'm sad to say we were underwhelmed by our experience. Awful street sellers
text: We arrived at the Colosseum to be met by countless street sellers which really spoiled the experience for us. They are beyond harassing and it made us so uncomfortable. On entering, the signage is not very clear if you have pre bought tickets and a tour. We just had to keep asking and eventually we were given a sticker and told to wait at a meeting point. The toilets are also pretty grim! The talk began in the waiting area before entering the Colosseum which took up the majority of it :S We were only inside for about 10 minutes before the tour ended but were allowed to stay and walk around. I just felt very underwhelmed. It was a very cold day so maybe that added to the feeling. The building is far more beautiful from the outside especially at night time. I wouldn't visit again unfortunately.

title: Desorganizado
text:
A construção, claro, é magnífica e nos deixa sem palavras. Além disso, conta com um metro bem em frente para quem não for ficar nos hotéis da região (pontos de ônibus também).
Adquirimos um passeio completo com guia que percorreu lugares internos inacessíveis com o ingresso normal, muito bom, recomendo!!
O único problema foi a desorganização, a entrada para esse passeio não possuía placas indicativas, mas uma fila que você poderia supor que fosse lá, depois de entrar não há nenhuma orientação de onde esperar e o que fazer, nosso guia também atrasou.
Então, fica a dica, se for fazer esse passeio, não fique esperando ajuda, pergunte, questione, se necessário mais de uma vez.

title: Long queue on free first sunday of the month
text: Free Sunday sounds good but long queue as a result.  Beware of tourist traps such as guided tours advertised to cut the queue.  They charge 15eur per person and cut no queue at all (we waited 1h30).

title: Ok
text: It's OK to say you've been but a long way down the list of what we enjoyed in Roma, big queues to get in when the best views are from outside!

title: quando sarà libero ...
text: una delle meraviglie della antichità arrivata sino a noi questo puo essere il titolo anche se la sua fama e bellezza è continuamente minata da interminabili lavori adiacenti e dalle sempre trafficate strade adiacenti... tempo fa era una gigante rotonda , ora va un po meglio ma... comunque rimane una calamita irrinunciabile oer qual si voglia visita a Roma

title: Muy lindo
text: Muy lindo como todo lo antiguo de Roma. Mucha gente y eso impide poder disfrutarlo a pleno. Pero es un placer estar frente a un pedazo de historia de la humanidad. Cara la entrada

title: At last
text:
Always wanted to visit Colosseum since I have always been amazed with Ancient Rome.

The weather was very bad when we were in cue, and the organization of the cue itself is really bad. My temper was tested plenty by all the sellers of umbrellas, ponchos and the so called official tourist guides that kept trying to have us pay 45€ to skip the line because they said it would take 3 hours from where we were standing, and this was on a day where the tickets were free (first Sunday of the month).

We were in within 40 minutes! So don’t fall for their trickery!

We spent less time inside the Colosseum than we did waiting inline mainly because the areas we hoped we would have access to were restricted, and require special tours. Not sure if they would be with it to be honest.

The Colosseum itself is a wonder and I am happy to have been there, but I believe once is enough, the images from movies give Colosseum more life and inspiration than a visit selfie-stick waving tourists and hoaxing “tourist”guides.

Veni, vidi, alibi

title: Colosseum scam
text: The lines to the Colosseum where extremely long and we were hassled by groups that wanted to get us in quicker at an extremely inflated rate.

title: Beautiful but i was expecting more
text: I cannot comment on the tour as we didn't go inside. We walked around and through the gardens, it is beautiful and a typical must see while in Rome, i wouldnt go back like other places we visited.

title: Beautiful but over rated
text:
Visited Rome with the wife for a weekend(colosseum was on my bucket list)
This is a difficult review to write for me because I love the place and the history etc but for myself it was kinda underwhelming if I’m totally honest! I would suggest unless you take a tour and get an in depth history lesson that you would be in and out within 1-2 hours if you really took your time! Am I glad I’ve been and seen it? Totally! Would I go again? Outside yes inside....errrm probably not if I’m honest! I think it’s a once you’ve seen it you’ve seen it situation. 
Still it’s an awe inspiring piece of history and I would recommend going if you’ve not been there.....I mean if your in Rome you can’t not go!!!! I’ll be back to Rome but not inside the coliseum.

title: un petit tour d'arène de Nimes
text:
Lieu certes chargé d'histoire, mais bien usé et peu commode pour déambuler.

Il serait bon de refaire vivre ces fastes et souffrances de gens condamnés par des vidéos

Un puy du fou à Rome serait passionnant et plus parlant pour la jeunesse

title: Big and beautiful
text:
Always a lot of people and lines at the Colosseum; book a tour online before arriving to be able to use the "fast line". I have visited with and without guide. There are some interesting facts you probably don't find in any guide books that you'll here of on a guided tour, so if you're interested in history I recommend that you book a guided tour. 
Worth a visit. Once. Then you've seen it; no need to return.

title: Changed over the years
text:
I came to the colosseum for the first time 7 years ago in the height of summer and it was lovely... busy as always but lovely.

However, this time was very different.

Whilst I expected it to be busy, I didn’t expect everyone who was selling something. Everywhere you turned someone was trying to sell a selfie stick, a tour, asking you to take part in a questionnaire. 

I was so overwhelmed I left. 

Absolutely ruins such a beautiful place. 

Wouldn’t recommend taking kids as it’s carnage!

title: Horrible experience

Outside of Colosseum there are a lot of private companies offering you to avoid line for around 35€ even though the ticket cost 12€. So although you pay €35 for a bunch of rocks or you stay in 2h cold for 12€. We were a bit disappointed since there was also some renovation work done at the bottom of the attraction.  I definitely do not recommend it from the inside however it is really spectacular and beautiful from the outside.

title: A lot of waiting around.
text: We arrived easily by Metro (1:50euros each) and then thought we would go around independently, but there are so many guides trying to sell you their tour that we surcomebed. 30 euros and the promise of a tour inside and a tour of Palantine Hill and the Forum. Even in January (low season) there is a lot of hanging around and queuing for security. There is climbing stairs and walking around with crowds and we didn't get to go to the underground area. It took about an hour. We then walked around independently looking at the exhibits and information boards. But we were still unable to go to the underground level. This was good value only when combined with the tour of the Palantine hill and Forum.

title: Was Once A Must See...Not Any More
text:
I've been to Rome many times starting back in the late 1970's. Back then and up until about the early 1990's The Colosseum was:
1) Free and easy to enter
2) Never too crowded except in peak season
3) Not full of people selling you Skip the Line Tickets or other hustles
4) Not Paying for photos with men dressed up like Gladiators. 

Now it's a tourist trap, hawkers paradise, overcrowded and COMPLETELY disorganized. No one knows where to queue inline to enter, the few guides that are there add to the confusion by telling people where to stand at first then only to tell them to go to another line. The arrival times for those who pre purchase tickets are meaningless. You can arrive on time only to have to wait as much as 1 1/2 hours more to get inside. 

It's very sad that it has come to this. I don't know of ANY other paid or free attraction in all of Italy that is run this poorly. 

Do yourself a favor, if you want to at least see the Colosseum arrive very early and just leisurely walk around the entire structure. The backside of the of the building actually offers some nice views.

title: Interesting to see, Not easy with a baby/toddler
text:
After experiencing the vatican museums the previous day, we thought it best to bring the baby sling with us to carry our 1 year old on our visit to the colosseum. Sadly there was no option to leave the buggy at the entrance desk so we still had to navigate with the stroller and baby in sling. Fortunately it was relatively quiet, 20 minute queue to buy tickets and were able to stroll around comfortably without crowds.
We opted for the audio guide to listen to the information while walking (rather than attempting to entertain our baby within a guided group), but it’s not possible to rewind any parts that we missed or couldn’t hear properly, and the volume could have been better on it. 
We Googled some facts about the history of the place, to fill in some gaps, and it is a breathtaking sight to see within the Colosseum walls.
We reckon it would be easier to visit without young children, especially if they’ll require the toilet facilities! They were awful. Set up in an old shipping container type thing and a baby change table in there but I would not put my child near it. It was in bad need of cleaning, the whole unit was, so try use facilities elsewhere either before or after the visit.

title: Красиво, но организация никакая
text:
Имейте в виду, что детский самокат (и возможно еще что-то) взять с собой нельзя, а камеры хранения нет никакой вообще и всем плевать, что ты будешь с этим делать. На Фору тоже. Хорошо хоть детскую коляску можно.
Организация никакая. Очереди переплетаются между собой, чтобы зайти нужно потратить кучу времени. Возможно, это из-за новогодних каникул, конечно. Создалось впечатление, что все сделано в Риме для того, чтобы человек пользовался услугами гида, потому что только они проходят без очередей, да и то не всегда. 
Процесс продажи билетов тоже ужасен. В очереди из 30 человек мы стояли минут 45 (2 кассира и это более или менее небольшая очередь у Форума). С детьми не пропускают без очереди, культурные и добрые иностранцы с моей просьбой дважды меня послали с двумя детьми и коляской. Постоянно влазят непонятные люди и покупают билеты минут по 15, хотя я на четверых купил билет за 1 минуту. Детей надо показывать кассиру, чтобы на них дали бесплатные билеты. Билеты в Колизей на определенное время, Форум и Палатин в этом же билете - можно 2 дня посещать и в любое время. У очереди все время терся один колоритный негр со своим другом 2 дня подряд, в разное время дня видели его там. Стоит то в очереди, то что-то как будто покупает. По факту либо ворует, либо что-то мутит, не поняли, но будьте начеку.
В общем, организация очень портит впечатление от этого великолепного сооружения.

title: Looks beautiful but not worth it
text: We visited the Colosseum in January 2019, and have to say it was a huge disappointment. The building itself is beautiful, however I found it strange that in a few places it was renovated with modern materials and style, which made it look a bit odd. We decided to go in and bought a ticket online, so luckily we did not need to queue. We arrived earlier than our time slot so we had to wait a while to get in. While we were waiting random people came to us about every 10 seconds asking if we want to go in, if we have tickets, trying to have a conversation clearly just to sell us a tour, others were coming to sell selfie sticks and other useless merchandise. The amount of people that came to us made the whole experience incredibly annoying, and by the time we could go in we just wanted to go home. Then came the slow and tedious security procedures, which further spoiled the Colosseum for us. All in all not a great experience, I don’t recommend going in.

title: Amazing if you don't mind being physically assaulted by the refugee peddlers and waiting in a huge line.
text: We visited the Colosseum in January and went on a tour provided by the Colosseum.  The tour and Colosseum was great.  So much great information and amazing sights.  However, there were no signs on where to meet for the tour, we had to talk with 3 different people to figure out how to pickup the tickets but thank goodness we booked the tour as the wait to get in for everyone else had to be hours long.  In addition, while waiting for my husband to go into the Colosseum to pick up the tickets (on the opposite side of the building from the normal entrance) my 15 year old son had a run in with a refugee immigrant trying to sell us something.  The man came up to us trying to sell us tickets or bracelets as about 50 others had while we walked around the structure, my son said no keep walking, the man went over to my son yelled in his face and stomped on his foot before finally leaving us alone.  Seriously this city is not safe and the peddlers are aggressive and make visiting the sites miserable. That combined with trash everywhere, human feces everywhere because were to all the refugees/homeless relieve them selves..on the streets and sidewalks, and pick pocketers made for Rome being the least favorite place I have ever been.  Save your time and money and go to Florence!

title: Overrated tours

title: It’s not fun, but you’d kick yourself for not doing it.
text:
The Xolosseum (or more properly, the Flavian Amphitheatre) is probably the definitive skyline of Rome. It’s been brilliantly restored, and the guiding services are first rate (at least the one we used was). You really can’t let yourself miss it, but I really can’t say I enjoyed it. Despite starting early in the morning in the middl of winter, we spent our time shuffling through a crowd of other tour groups and the throng of unguided visitors, jostling for space, and fstruggling not to be left behind at the choke points. If you take on the package of colosseum, Palatine Hill and Forum, you’ll really appreciate hitting the open space of the bigger archeological area.
Despite all that, could you go to Rome and NOT visit the Colosseum?

title: Very disappointing!!!
text:
We had high expectation for this place but if you have the patience of listening to hundreds of tour guides who want to sell you tickets outside before you go in and people who try to sell you other things that can be quite aggressive then it really makes your mood quite low.

Also be prepared to go through security scanners before entering, we had a time slot and could not enter until 10 mins before our time, you still have to go through security even if you skip the queue but skipping the queue is worth it as the normal queue for the colosseum is huge so definitely worth having your ticket adjusted.

What was the most annoying is that there were police there but wasn’t doing anything to stop the people selling stuff as this is actually illegal. 

If you don’t experience any of this then I’m sure it will be great.

title: Very long security lines in high holiday season
text: We purchased "skip the line" tickets, but learned that that is somewhat deceptive since there wasn't a way to skip the long, long security lines. I think the best bet may be to pay more for a small tour group (that seem to enter through higher-priority entrances or arrive with pre-purchased tickets as soon as lines open in the morning.

Hay unas colas descomunales y muy mala información ya que no está en paneles o carteles, solo los informadores te la dan y a veces es contradictoria y te cambian de fila    Según consideren, q aun no sabemos por qué.
Aunq tengas la entrada tienes que canjearla x un bono, cosa q tampoco sabíamos ni nos informamos al comprar la entrada. En general, creo q ayudarían carteles explicativos en varios idiomas.

title: Spettacolare Opera ma organizzazione da dimenticare
text:
Che peccato: arrivi con la metro, scendi alla fermata Colosseo e ti trovi davanti cotanta imponenza (a parte il cantiere enorme della Metro)... poi purtroppo arrivi in piazza e c’e’ di tutto: pessime indicazioni turistiche (dove vengono venduti i biglietti ufficiali DEVE essere chiaramente indicato molte volte); i turisti sono in balia dei “bagarini saltacoda”, si capisce poco e chiedono cifre astronomiche: un furto che avviene sotto l’occhio distratto e/o compiacente di chi dovrebbe vigilare. 
I varchi con metal detector sono ridicoli, pochi e malgestiti e la coda nasce tutta li.
Il Colosseo e’ stupendo ma lasciarlo in mano ai barbari fu un peccato duemila anni fa e lo e’ anche oggi.

title: Coliseu
text:
Lugar maravilhoso. Mas extremamente cheio de gente, desorganizado. 
Emocionante estar em um lugar que possui uma história como está.  Onde estiveram tantos e por séculos ainda estarão...

title: Beware of the "Vultures"
text: Go to the Colosseum... book your visit online.  Once you get off the Metro you will be greeted by people selling merchandise and tours.  You can't go 2 feet without someone selling you something.  The most frustrated place in Rome... be prepared and have everything in advance!  I love the tour... hated getting from the Metro to the entrance!

title: So busy!!
text:
Arrived in Rome late December and paid a visit to what is a must see attraction.

It was however very busy and I would recommend planning your visit properly and buying tickets in advance of your visit. This at least let's you skip the main queue although still took an hour to get in. 

Beware of the Kenyan gangs looking to give you presents (In exchange for money). Starts off with a handshake...

Bear advice us to keep your hands in your pockets and walk on. As soon as you engage in conversation you are trapped.

Very irritating also was the scarf, water, selfie stick sellers who were in your faces as soon as you arrive. I was quite pleased to be called a bastardo after ignoring one of them!

Definitely worth a visit but keep your wits about you

title: No vale la pena
text:
No vale la pena pagar para entrar y hacer cola por 2 horas.
Solo de fuera ya se puede observar todo su esplendor

title: Una vergüenza la desorganización
text: Fuimos el 31 de diciembre. Nos acercamos a la fila para los que ya tenían entradas a las 13:45. Calculamos que entraríamos por la cantidad de gente que había. Durante los primeros 45 minutos la cola avanzaba. Luego dejó de moverse porque la gente iba llegando y al ver el gentío se metía por adelante sin respetar la fila. No había carriles ni nadie del lugar que pusiera orden de ningún tipo! Conclusión: a las 3:30 cerraron el ingreso y nos quedamos afuera. Una falta de respeto que no haya una mínima organización.

title: Spettacolo eterno ma con qualche limite
text: Sul Colosseo credo ci sia poco da raccontare di nuovo. La struttura è ben curata ma l'accesso è troppo lento. Un'ora e mezza di coda è veramente tanto, anche se credo sia difficile trovare una soluzione. Consigliabile l'acquisto on line dei biglietti, validi per Colosseo e Palatino

title: must see in Rome
text: magnificent, must see attraction. We pre booked tickets and has a guide. interesting. bit of a queue to go through security.

title: Deludente
text: Coda infinita , ma grazie al biglietto combinato con i fori abbiamo evitato la fila. Entrati siamo rimasti delusi, le aspettative erano più alte. Indubbiamente da fuori, invece, ha un aspetto maestoso.

title: non puoi passare da Roma senza visitare il Colosseo ma che delirio all'entrata
text: nonostante avessimo acquistato i biglietti online (voucher) quando arrivi è piuttosto complicato capire dove devi cambiare i vouchers con i biglietti e poi devi comunque informarti nella bolgia dove fare la fila; insomma, il classico mucchio selvaggio dove devi barcamenarti

title: Très beau site à visiter, mais un accueil à améliorer ...
text:
Le Colisée est un incontournable de Rome. On peut faire le tour de tout l’édifice avec différentes plaques qui nous rappellent l’Histoire chargée du Colisée. Très belle conservation du batiment. 

Dommage que l’entrée coupe-file soit mal indiquée. Un bémol également pour les contrôles de sécurité. Alors que nous n’avions aucune explication, nous sommes faits réprimander EN ITALIEN par les agents. Et quand nous nous excusons en expliquant que nous ne comprenons pas ce que l’on nous dit, on nous regarde agacé en continuant de plus belle...

title: Πρωτοχρονιά 2019
text: Όμορφο τοπίο. Δεν χρειάζεται να πληρώσεις για να μπεις μέσα. Αρκεί να βγάλεις ωραίες φωτογραφίες....

title: ein muss auf jeden Fall
text: ein perfekter start für sightseeing, sehr imposant aber die langen schlangen vor dem Eingang schrecken dann doch ab es zu besuchen, aber auch von Aussen jeden Blick wert

title: 混みすぎで入れず
text:
12/31の朝、フォロ・ロマーノ側のチケット売り場でチケットを買い、午前中はフォロ・ロマーノを観光し、13:30頃からコロッセオの列に並び始めました。ローマパスや既にチケットを買っている人は、チケットを買う列には並ばないので簡単に入れるものと思いましたが、それでも2時間待ち。ひどい混雑でした。
この日は15:30が最終入場で、並んでいても間に合わない可能性があるため、友人は+15€払ってガイド付きツアーに参加（列をスキップできる）、私は諦めて帰りました。

title: Coupe fil Mont Palatin
text:
Nous avons visité le Colisée et avions réservé 2 billets " Coupe fil " qui incluait la visite du Colisée ainsi que le Mont Palantin, le forum..
Pour le Colisée, pas de soucis..nous nous somme rendus dans la file dédiée et sommes passés rapidement mais en arrivant pour la visite du Mont Palatin, pas de file réservée !! Il fallait faire la queue!!!
Très déçus !! Surtout quand on paie 20€ par personne!!!!

title: Grandiose but nit a nice experience
text: Yes it needs to be seen, yes it is majestic, very well restored, but the amount of people they let in, the mess to have information on how to get in, the way groups are managed, it just kills the experience...

title: Awestruck but dissapointed
text: Such a beautiful structure, totally spoiled by the army of "guides" (should be renamed as scammers, touts) and the amount of street vendors constantly bothering the tourists. I hate to think what this is like in the summer.

title: Un assalto!
text:
È senza dubbio uno dei monumenti da visitare almeno una volta nella vita ma sul contorno stendiamo un velo pietoso. Già appena messo piede fuori dalla metro (e sei col naso in su ad ammirare questa meraviglia) vieni letteralmente circondato da venditori di tour/saltafila e gadget vari. Noi avevamo già il biglietto saltafila con prenotazione oraria ma non ci sono indicazioni su dove ritirare i biglietti d'ingresso. Ci facciamo spazio tra turisti, guide e venditori cercando le indicazioni della biglietteria giusta e dopo un primo smarrimento, la troviamo e...ci mettiamo in coda con gli altri prenotati! Assurdo fare 40 minuti di coda per dei biglietti "saltafila". Inoltre sul voucher era indicato di presentarsi alla biglietteria soltanto 15 minuti prima dell'orario di ingresso previsto...menomale che noi, essendo arrivati 1 ora prima ci siamo messi comunque in fila! Una volta presi i biglietti ci viene indicato l'ingresso (peccato fosse in mezzo  alla fila di ingresso gruppi e alla fila dei non prenotati quindi farsi spazio per accedere alla nostra fila non è stato semplice). Una volta "incanalati" passiamo sotto il controllo del metal detector e finalmente dopo 1 ora siamo dentro!Non oso immaginare i tempi di attesa per i non prenotati (la fila era interminabile!).
Una volta dentro però, nonostante la gente, è vivibile. Si visita prima il secondo piano (dove ci sono 2 mostre molto interessanti) e il piano terra. Noi non abbiamo preso l'audioguida ma avendo una buona guida turistica (della Rough Guide) e grazie anche ai molti cartelli espositivi (soprattutto nella mostra) siamo rimasti soddisfatti delle spiegazioni. Purtroppo abbiamo rinunciato all'ingresso ai fori romani perché la fila era molto lunga e, anche facendola, non saremmo riusciti ad entrare entro l'orario consentito (avremmo rischiato di fare più di 1 ora di coda per poi essere rimbalzati). Le cose che secondo me andrebbero migliorate sono 2: 
- dividere i biglietti per il colosseo e per i fori (perché non tutti sono interessati ai fori ma se vendi  un biglietto comulativo è normale che la gente voglia entrare al foro creando code inverosimili!)
- il biglietto comulativo vale per 2 giorni consecutivi ma devi prima necessariamente visitare il colosseo e poi accedere ai fori. Perché??? Inoltre, per chi come me, ha acquistato il biglietto per il 31 dicembre (prezzo pieno, non scontato...) non ha potuto utilizzarlo il giorno dopo, cioè il primo gennaio perché i monumenti sono chiusi... Un po' una fregatura...

title: Great place to visit, but avoid the skip the line vendors in particular “Gladiator Tours”
text:
This is an amazing and unbelievable site to see, from inside and out. The lines were extremely long. Make sure you get your tickets before had or get there early for general admission. (we did a guided tour, with a company called Gladiator Tours.)
They promised to skip the lines but in the end we waited longer than if we had just paid a general admission. The tour guide was appallingly unprofessional, answering his phone numerous times, and mocking the delayed entry. The audio was terrible and you could hardly understand what he was saying. It was extremely disappointing and we almost asked for our money back, while we were waiting in the line... which he said we could do. But in the end I didn’t want to line up again to get in. 

I highly recomend you book online before you travel. Getting them from the official site is best. Ignore all the people telling you to "skip the line". The guided tour allowed you access to the top floors, with spectacular views.

title: Una coda spaventosa ...e chi ti offre i saltacoda.....boh
text: ogni tanto chiudono l’accesso per il numero di turisti all’interno. La coda è snervante. Consiglio la prenotazione!

title: restée sur ma faim
text: Il faut absolument y aller avec des billets déjà acheté. En plein été ce ne doit même pas être vivable. Attention lieu bondé de touristes, mais celà fait parti des incontournables de Rome (attention les Nimois, ne perdez pas de temps à y aller, vos arênes sont nettement plus belles, à mon avis.... de Montpelliéraine).

title: ETERNITY QUEING UP WITH RESERVATIONS...IN THE ETERNAL CITY...
text:
We booked online about a month  before, in order to AHEM...beat the er...queues?!!?
We went in December...and despite booking online to beat the queue, we had to queue for over an hour initially, then we get told to come back between 2 to 4 (It was around 12).
We went off for lunch and as we didn't  trust the people in the ticket office a single bit, decided to go around 2pm.
Oh and then another  half an hour queing-despite having already got the so called beat the queue tickets.
Also the queues for reservations were almost mixed up with pay on the day, so much so that some airhead, who's sole purpose in life is to flirt her way through queues managed to jump the queue in front of us-and she was without reservations!
When we did manage to get inside, there was also a long queue for audio guide collection, as we'd opted for this, but since we'd been queuing for near enough eternity, we decided to not waste time, queuing yet again for audio guides.
Of course it was crowded inside, but we were lucky to only queue for around 1.5 hours in total DESPITE jump the queue options. 
So beware in the winter if you visit the Colosseum for your reservations won't  really get you very far. 
Also bear in mind hardly anything is sign posted, you'd  think that such an important and world known historical sight would have directions, over where to go, but forget it...
In all honesty just get off at Coloseo metro and take pictures from outside, for inside there will be many people, which of course will ruin the experience for you.
Makes one wonder what really contributed towards the decline of the Roman Empire...

title: Une organisation à revoir fortement
text:
Mon avis porte que l’organisation de la visite et non, bien sûr, sur la valeur historique du Colisée. Certes, il y a, surtout les week-ends de vacances, le monde qui conflue à la porte du monument. Mais c’est le cas de chacunes des icônes touristiques en Europe. Le Colisée se distingue en ce qu’il ne montre pas le souci d’organiser d’une quelconque manière cette masse. L’institution est singulièrement anarchique. Les visiteurs, qu’ils aient ou non un billet en avance (horaires ou non), en groupe ou individuellement, s’amassent eux-mêmes devant les trois portes (groupes/billets payés/billetterie). Ils finissent donc par former trois files sans organisation, peu ou pas distinguées. Il n’y a pas d’information ou de personnel disponible, ce qui oblige les patients à s’en référer aux vendeurs de coupe-file pour avoir quelque idée de ce qui se passe. Pas de caisses automatiques, d’entrée rapide, ou de réservation régulée en ligne : tout ceux qui le veulent s’amassent, et entrera qui pourra. 
En conséquence, les temps d’attente sont intenables : compter plus de 2 heures le week-end ou durant les vacances, jusqu’à l’infini et au-delà. Il n’est pas rare d’attendre toute l’après-midi, et de se voir refuser l’entrée, sans, du reste, plus de politesse que de fermer une barrière, sans un mot, devant les visiteurs. En hiver, l’entrée est fermée à 15h30 : il faut aussi impérativement arriver le matin.
Le Colisée est en ce sens un cas d’école de mauvaise gestion touristique, qui ne fait honneur ni au monument, ni à la ville. L’écrasante majorité des institutions touristiques européennes ont réussi à dépasser les problèmes de régulations des entrées qui se posaient dans les années 1990 et 2000 : le Colisée nous ramène à cette période. Il coute du reste peu de forcer la réservation horaire en avance, mais le manque de moyen du ministère de la culture est probablement pour quelque chose dans l’état de cette institution.

title: A must!
text:
Must see it! 

That's it!

As all Rome it felt quite busy and not so clean in the streets compared to other Italian or International cities.

Of course Rome is a Huge city with Millions of tourists, but that cannot be always the excuse.

title: Interesting history of a bloody entertainment site !
text: I dunno . It is a very old structure flooded with tourists. It was completed in the yr 80 AD !  That is old .  The whole forum area surrounding the coliseum is very very old also . The Italians have maintained their relics remarkably well.  From what our guide said , it was built to keep the blood thirsty residents of Rome entertainined and occupied, so they wouldn’t revolt on the current emperor and pope ! .?  It was gruesome murder of slaves that the armies took in their battles !  This is perhaps more visited than the Vatican and St Peter’s Basilca, said our guide .  Hard to believe I thought .  It is amazing to think you are standing in a place where incredible murders were carried out as entertainment for years . I dunno .  It is definitely worth seeing since you are in Rome , but St Peter’s is way way more incredible !

title: Skip the Line
text: we booked an official „skip the line“ group tour. well it still took more than 1 1/2 hours to get in for 35€ each! Tour Guide (Italian) - photo - was great! but don‘t expect immediate entrance!

title: Waste of money!
text:
Our skip the line tickets were useless. Bought 2 afternoon tickets to see the Colosseum, forums and Palatine hill. We arrive as instructed at 1pm at our meeting spot (Roman empire) only to be told to come back at 2:20pm with little information as to why. So we hung around and came back at 2:10pm. We then waited for another 20 minutes and then got told to go to the line. No help or guide to show us where to go. Then we preceded to wait in line for an 1 hour. By this time we only had time to see the colloseum before it closed and missed out on the rest. Incredibly disappointed, the staff were incredibly unorganized and will not bother going through this process again. I understand there can be a language barrier but I don't think that can really be an excuse in this situation. 

The Colosseum itself is worth visiting, I'd just recommend the morning session so you can allow for more time, before everything closes. And just buy regular tickets. Skip the line is a joke and would only work for venues that didn't attract as many people. You buy a skip the line ticket and then go and wait in line with a couple of hundred people who did the same.

title: Superbe mais attention à l’organisation !!
text:
Cet endroit est magique mais attention au tour opératif que vous choisirez!!!!
Pour nous Musement n’a pas été à la hauteur du tout : rdv donné dans une boutique à 8:20 (fermée en fait jusqu’à 9:30 le jour de notre visite), attente devant le Colisée pendant 20 minutes une fois les personnes de Musement retrouvées à 300m du point de rencontre initial, pas d’audio guides alors que c’était prévu (rembourse 5€/personne alors que cela coûte 5,5€ : ce n’est pas pour le prix mais pour le principe!), perte de temps pour récupérer les audioguides a l’intérieur (queue avec tout le monde alors que nous avions opté pour des coupe files pour justement éviter tout cela), RDV à la sortie pour aller sur le mont Palatin et au forum non tenu (3 familles sur le carreau à attendre) alors que nous étions bien tous au lieu indiqué à l’heure précise (beaucoup de monde et la personne qui était en orange vif au début de la visite a eu la bonne idée de mettre une doudoune noire : c’est tellement plus voyant dans la foule!!!!!).
Bref, un lieu impressionnant et auquel l’organisation « foireuse de Musement » n’a rien réussi à enlever tellement c’est à voir!

title: Do not consider a visit without a guide
text: Went on a Roma pass without a guide and that was a mistake.  Unfortunately it was a bit rainy too...so we cut the self tour short and really there isn't much to tell you what you are seeing and the relevance of such.  Our fault...but really there is so much more to know that you will not know without a guide.  It is awesome to look at but would be more memorable if you could have an inkling as to the history of this well known site.
